# Experiment history

Navigation: [current state](STATUS.md), [candidate routes](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md),
[archived status](STATUS_HISTORY_20261105.md). New entries should identify the idea,
tested tuple, outcome/limits, evidence, decision and what would justify revisiting.
Record meaningful attempts rather than every monitoring update.

Search for relevant prior attempts before optimization work. Add a row for a meaningful result, not every run. Scope and evidence limit each result; a prior outcome does not prohibit a changed approach. Historical records were archived during the 2026-10-31 documentation cleanup at `/home/philip/shaderlod-doc-archive-20261031/docs-and-agent-setup.tar.gz`; this index is not yet exhaustive. The archive is local to this machine and is not in Git.

**Current direction (2026-11-08 Pacific):** [STATUS](STATUS.md#latest-outcome-and-next-action)
is authoritative. Retention requires a positive result across all four supported
shaders and both completed machines (Asahi and RTX 5080). None qualified;
G01–G10, C01–C02 and N01–N04 are all parked, with no default enablement.
Historical gains, implementations and evidence remain preserved. The next useful
engineering direction is the [cost-map extension sketch](COST_MAP.md), not more
G-number optimizations. This documentation decision adds no measurements.

**Historical campaign disposition (2026-11-01; superseded as current direction):** the user resumed sustained optimization/review, excluding C02. Ten finite local searches (G01/G03/G04/G05/G06/G07/G08/G09/G10/C01) are independently closed; G02’s viable routes are complete and its remaining Complementary native startup is blocked, with a fresh independent CLOSE stopping review. Default enablement remains unqualified; [STATUS](STATUS.md) is authoritative. Historical “CLOSE” and “complete” labels refer to the assigned implementation/evaluation/report scope, not exhausted optimization potential. Rejected routes retain their negative evidence; inconclusive and hardware/input/compatibility-blocked items are not blanket net-negative results. Historical rows describing active work or pending checks reflect their capture time. That historical quick-test pause was superseded by the later sustained-work request.

**Historical N01–N04 campaign (2026-11-02):** all four have independent CLOSE verdicts for the finite research scope. Candidates remain private/default-off with compatibility limits and blockers recorded. These historical closures do not close the new cross-shader/cross-machine audit. ## Declared affected pass graph and certificate storage

All three declared targets and both pass viewports resolve to full rendered
dimensions. The producer draws logical **0/2**; the consumer draws **0/3**, with
the original conditional target-0-only branch also declared.

| Logical target | Format | Declared quantity roles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `R11F_G11F_B10F` | GENERAL completed original scene RGB, 3 channels |
| 2 | `RGBA32F` | Linear basis, 4 channels; bounded exact binary32 integers, 3 channels; binary32 minimum distance, 1 channel |
| 3 | `RGBA8` | GENERAL original auxiliary data, 4 channels |

Quantity views occupy different texels and their channel requirements are not
summed. In each 2 × 2 tile, `(0,0)` stores the four-component canonical-white
diffuse/AO-shadow basis, `(1,0)` stores
`(epoch, quantity_side_token, tile_linear_index, minimum_distance_blocks)`, and
the other lanes are invalid. Exact integer magnitude is explicitly bounded by
`2^24`: epoch `[0, 2^24]`, token `258`, tile index `[0, 2^24 - 1]`. Direct minimum
distance uses binary32. Surface dimensions must be `[2,8192]` per axis; thus CEIL
half-tile capacity is at most `2^24`. Integer texelFetch is declared for these
reads. The unchanged source guards reject mismatched texture dimensions, epoch,
certificate, invalid/nonfinite quantity and partial odd-edge tiles.

# Benchmark guide

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test \
  --profile /path/to/prepared/client \
  --pack /path/to/original-pack.zip \
  --pack-options /path/to/original-pack.zip.txt \
  --feature PUBLIC_OPTIMIZATION_ID \
  --output /path/to/fresh/report
```

On Linux ARM64 use `python3 scripts/linux_arm64_runtime.py benchmark test` with the same arguments. Select an existing loader/version/scene slot; keep the report outside that slot and on the same filesystem as the profile. Confirm the lane is free and the inputs match the intended tuple before launch. Do not reset a slot owned by a client or interrupted operation. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout --help` describes managed checkout. Use `run_storage.copytree` for profile/world copies; it enforces storage limits.

The standard test targets the prepared NeoForge 1.21.1 benchmark protocol. It acquires native Off, singleton candidate through normal Apply, then native Off return: 20 seconds each, with separate warmup, startup and recovery. It records total-frame timing, drift, stills and restoration in the report. A valid slower result is still a result; a failed or invalid run is not a speed conclusion. Inspect `summary.json`, errors and restoration before proceeding. A short result is not proof of visual equivalence, DH/PBR compatibility or final closure. Compare matched total-frame measurements and disclose drift and scope.

If the harness or inputs fail, preserve the failure, restore/release owned resources, fix the maintained harness or inputs, and retry. Do not copy harness code into report-local callers, inject launcher overrides, relax admission after failure, or substitute custom scripts for the standard result. Diagnostics are diagnostic and do not replace it. The standard command's end-to-end behavior on the current setup has not yet been independently verified; do not claim otherwise.

Keep reports, worlds, downloads, builds and captures out of Git. Do not kill unrelated processes. If restoration refuses due to unknown changes, preserve the data and inspect ownership and recovery before acting.

## Required comparisons

For each case and block, pair all selected stack combinations: minimal versus
optimized, minimal versus optimized-culling, and optimized versus
optimized-culling when all three are selected. Report each block's percent time
reduction, then the median, range and median absolute deviation across independent
JVM blocks. A positive reduction means less time. Do not pool frames across
launches or compute confidence intervals from autocorrelated frames. GPU render
intervals, CPU wall/thread clocks, FPS-derived frame duration and each run's p95
remain separate metrics. Repeated blocks reduce order drift but do not establish
simultaneous controls; partial Williams cycles do not fully balance position.

Every case × selected stack × block must exist exactly once, with complete runs
and a complete matrix status. Each run needs a unique valid UUID, matching
manifest/report requests, unique retained measurement/summary paths, and UTC
capture/write timestamps inside its launch interval. Launch intervals may not
overlap. Recomputed retained-sample metrics must match the saved summary. An
invalid or failed run rejects the whole matrix; rerun into a fresh directory
instead of filtering it out. New manifests should declare `cases` and `stacks`
independently of their run rows. Legacy stack selection inferred from rows cannot
detect removal of every row of an entire stack; this limit is reported explicitly.

Hold these inputs identical within a case, across stacks **and across blocks**:

- Exact shader archive SHA256 and complete loaded Iris effective option map,
  including every `SHADERLOD_` option; requested settings and recorded option
  hashes must agree. Lower quality is a separate case.
- ShaderLOD/DH presence, loaded base-mod versions and loaded artifact SHA256s.
  Mandatory Minecraft/NeoForge/Iris/Sodium identities must be present. Only
  locked optimizer mods and their explicit locked embedded mods may differ.
- Fixed source-world SHA256, actual dimension, camera, weather/time, framebuffer,
  requested and effective detail radii, live LOD settings and feature activity.
- Semantic Iris properties and DH TOML. Comment/order-only rewrites are harmless
  when their captured content verifies equivalence. Complete loaded ShaderLOD
  semantics may replace raw config identity; ordinary captures lacking them
  conservatively require equal raw config SHA256 and live LOD snapshots.
- Measurement request, actual warmup, GPU backend, sampling cadence and remaining
  runtime instrumentation properties. Shader wetness must match: fixed controls
  require observed suppliers applying the requested value at both boundaries and
  throughout capture; dynamic controls need equal observed wetness boundaries and
  applied ranges. World rain alone is insufficient.
- Available window observations: stable focus/visibility/minimization, window
  and framebuffer sizes, vsync, fullscreen, focus-pause policy and configured
  frame limit. Reject capture transitions, unavailable observations, hidden or
  minimized windows, and unfocused windows with focus-pause enabled. Counts and

  older captures without window telemetry are accepted only with an explicit

## Measurement scope and stopping rules

The existing harness changes only live global enable, holding one archive,
world, pipeline and policy in one JVM. OFF retains the same volume integration
graph; it is not original Photon/mod absent. The method therefore screens
incremental existing-pass budget cost only. World/pipeline reference checks run
inside the client; raw object identities are not exported for independent replay.

Capture FPS is actual counted render frames divided by elapsed capture seconds;
mean total-frame duration is elapsed seconds × 1,000 / render frames. This
includes scheduling, driver submission, swap/events and pacing. GPU `game-render`
is an instrumented timeline interval, not utilization or total frame time.
Apple M3 Max uses asynchronous elapsed queries; no timestamp or physical work
count acceptance follows. GPU frame-only N5/coarse CPU must remain identical
through every phase. Minimum 60 positive finite unique full-render observations,
valid frame/epoch bounds, no epoch reuse, at least 20 seconds per phase and exact
window/source/config/temporal guards stay required. Quiet captures exclude
builds, tests, encoders and unrelated worker CPU work.

OFF/ON/OFF/ON gives two adjacent contrasts, always in the same order. Same-JVM
pairing removes restart regime changes but does not cancel monotonic host drift,
thermal behavior, temporal shader state or autocorrelation. An absolute OFF
frame/GPU drift above 10% is inconclusive; both GPU directions must agree with
both total-frame improvements. The final preregistered screen requires at least
5% lower mean total-frame duration in both pairs (5.263% higher FPS). The runtime
owner corrected the initial runner's FPS-denominator discrepancy before any
preparation or launch, with a boundary fixture rejecting 52.6 versus 50 FPS:
that is 5.2% more FPS but only 4.943% lower frame duration. Report both denominators
and do not retroactively change the screen.

Four end-of-phase PNGs can reject gross cloud/lighting corruption; they do not
establish pixel parity, motion quality, transitions, flicker, water/reflection or
thin-feature fidelity. Real loaded options and source qualification are distinct
from linked shader uniform consumption, physical iteration counts and quality.
Even a passing screen still needs balanced repeated original/mod-absent,
patched-disabled and enabled controls plus representative still/motion and
second-workload checks before any substantial gain/default promotion claim.

## One chain and transition result algebra

W=0 uses d<near full, near≤d<far middle and d≥far far. Positive W centers bands
at near/far: [near-W/2,near+W/2] and [far-W/2,far+W/2]. For96/160/W8 these are
92..100 and156..164. Full near output is assured through the lower edge; the
near transition straddles the ideal near threshold. Valid widths prevent overlap.
Smoothstep weights require no temporal noise or new accumulation assumption.
Equal adjacent budgets collapse to one count/result; pure weights return the
endpoint directly. Smooth weights do not guarantee moving-hit quality.

On an eligible first hit inside the native refinement cutoff, classify the
originating viewPos and run one original midpoint chain. Preserve the initial
oldPos/curPos bracket and every original a/b update. Capture UV/depth at the
needed counts2/3/4. Mode1 always4. Mode2 always4 even when the returned result
uses count2 or3; it is a transition-quality diagnostic. Mode3 stops at maximum
needed count; pure2/3 can avoid two/one depth refinements. Near4 and a4→lower
transition still execute4. Misses/cutoff failures do no policy work and keep
their native return. There is no second complete SSR trace or path blend.

Evaluate one endpoint color outside a genuine unequal-count transition, at
most two inside one; each endpoint independently preserves the native final
depth guard/vignette/fresnel. Invalid-hit endpoints return native zero RGBA.
For a transition, blend premultiplied reflected RGB contribution and opacity,
then divide contribution by nonzero opacity to reconstruct the native return.
Exactly zero opacity returns zero; pure endpoint weights return that endpoint
without reconstruction. Nonzero signed opacity is not silently clamped, retaining
the algebraic native composition contract. For physical nonnegative opacities,
zero implies no contribution. A signed cancellation with nonzero contribution
cannot be represented by native zero-alpha RGBA and is outside qualified
physical endpoint assumptions; quality inspection must catch abnormal values.

Independent fixtures compare the original caller's composed color against the
weighted composition of both endpoint results, including valid-to-miss and
both-zero cases. Straight independent RGB/alpha interpolation is deliberately
not used, avoiding the artificial darkening of valid-to-miss blending.

## Shared operation and explicit consumers

[refinement_budget.glsl](../patches/adapters/shared/refinement_budget.glsl) defines
`shaderlod_refinement_budget(bridge, enabled, preset, distance_blocks, original, minimum)`.
It changes only the count of existing refinements after a coarse crossing is found.
It does not shorten primary coarse traversal, rescale ray increments, multiply
radiance/alpha, replace a fallback or create new texture fetches. It is a reusable
operation, and a future Photon consumer would need an explicit valid-crossing
refinement site with its original count and floor, not a generic shader rewrite.
The portable performance worker owns the separate raster `render_budget.glsl`;
these adapters do not include that helper because the inspected packs have no
matching, reviewed TAAU raster-scale graph.

The shared helper validates core bridge 2 and exact enabled/preset values. Preset
0 retains at least 87.5% of original refinements, presets 1/2 at least 75%, using
conservative ceiling and floor 4. Distance is camera-relative Euclidean blocks;
upstream `lViewPos` in Complementary, `length(hitPoint)` in MakeUp. Full work
through 96 blocks, smooth request transition to 192 blocks, rounded count beyond.
These distances are fixed source policy for this candidate; advanced mod near/far
controls do not currently change them. Integer refinement thresholds may pop.
There is no frame-dependent selector or temporal sampling addition.

Shader option `SHADERLOD_REFINEMENT_ADAPTER` defaults to 0 and appears under a new
ShaderLOD option screen, leaving upstream profiles intact. With option 0 the
inserted helper/uniform consumer code is excluded. Option 1 declares and consumes
existing Iris transport names `shaderlodBridgeVersion`, `shaderlodEnabled`, and
`shaderlodPreset`. Missing/invalid transport, global Off and QUALITY preset 3
all retain original counts. Core uniform registration exists in the mod source;
actual loaded options and producer-to-consumer linkage require runtime proof.
Reload after changing option/preset/enabled controls until history is checked.

Complementary Reimagined/Unbound r5.9.3 share byte-identical `reflections.glsl`.
Their explicit patch budgets `refinementCount` only in `GBUFFERS_WATER`; its
original 30/38 coarse-sample limits, loop geometry, error/hit tests, sky fallback
and surface brightness remain unchanged. Composite PBR reflections are protected.
Balanced with original count 6 rounds back to 6, so that branch saves no work.
MakeUp keeps `RAYMARCH_STEPS=10` and all coarse-search iterations. It increments
a local refinement counter only when upstream `searchFlag` is true; it can break

Fewer refinements are not equivalent results: ray hit position/validity can change,
including reflected structures or glass. Near-field full counts and unchanged
brightness/fallback do not prove low visual loss. These candidates need actual

# Development camera quality capture

`src/devClient/java/com/pp/shaderlod/dev/CameraQualitySession.java` is the integrated
development capture utility. It compiled and completed bounded runtime smokes
recorded below; broader quality acceptance remains pending.
The GPU/client owner must review, integrate, compile and inspect actual moving

source and this document; common protocol code, existing harnesses, shader
sources, build configuration and client processes are untouched.

The harness addresses the missing moving-camera quality check for original,
derivative-off and derivative-on packs. It records quality evidence only.

## Activation and integration

Only `shaderlod.dev.cameraQuality` activates it. Its value is the path of a
local JSON request, read once and limited to 64 KiB. An absent/blank property
returns `null` without opening files, creating threads or moving the player.
`shaderlod.dev.cameraQualityOnly=true` additionally authorizes stopping this
same client after the final manifest and PNG callback handling. The session
must have acquired its local spectator UUID; a rejected request does not close
an unacquired client.

The runtime owner can copy the reviewed file into
`src/devClient/java/com/pp/shaderlod/dev/CameraQualitySession.java`. Keep it in
the dev client source set and ensure it remains absent from the production jar.
Small hooks in `ComparisonClient` are sufficient:

```java
private CameraQualitySession cameraQuality;

// In the existing one-time configured block, after scene/control preparation:
cameraQuality = CameraQualitySession.createIfRequested(
        client.gameDirectory.toPath());

// After applyControl() in ClientTickEvent.Post, before normal workload handling:
if (cameraQuality != null) {
    cameraQuality.tick(client);
    GpuTimers.drainSamples();
    CpuTimers.drainSamples();
    return;
}

// At the START of draw(RenderGuiEvent.Post), before hideGui's early return:
if (cameraQuality != null) {
    event.getGuiGraphics().flush();
    cameraQuality.render(Minecraft.getInstance());
}
```

before both old manual/automatic screenshot schedules. The configured block

## Request example and path behavior

This 24-second example starts at the existing noDH shoreline player position.
It is an example, not an executed or quality-approved trajectory. Place it in
an ignored prepared runtime directory and use the same request bytes for all
pack arms. The first waypoint must match the prepared `control.json` position
and yaw/pitch within 0.05 blocks/0.1 degrees. Coordinates are **player feet**;
captured `mainCamera` coordinates include the actual interpolated eye height.

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "label": "shoreline-motion-r1",
  "warmupSeconds": 30,
  "fps": 10,
  "waypoints": [
    {"seconds": 0,  "x": 240.5, "y": 68.0, "z": 680.5, "yaw": -180.0, "pitch": 3.0},
    {"seconds": 8,  "x": 244.5, "y": 68.0, "z": 668.5, "yaw": -165.0, "pitch": 5.0},
    {"seconds": 16, "x": 236.5, "y": 69.0, "z": 672.5, "yaw": -195.0, "pitch": 2.0},
    {"seconds": 24, "x": 240.5, "y": 68.0, "z": 680.5, "yaw": -180.0, "pitch": 3.0}
  ]
}
```

Labels accept 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, underscores and hyphens. The source
is parsed to immutable records; exact raw source bytes and their SHA-256 are
retained. The original request is rehashed with bounded reads once each second
and at finalization. Changing it fails the session.

Waypoints number 2–32 and start at time zero. All values must be numeric and
finite. X/Z are within ±29,999,000, Y within ±2048, yaw within ±3600 and pitch
within ±90 degrees. Segment duration is at least 0.25 seconds; total duration is
20–30 seconds and total travel at most 512 blocks. The frame rate is an integer
1–10, and duration must end on a capture slot. Peak eased movement/rotation is
limited to 32 blocks/s and 90 degrees/s. Yaw is unwrapped along the shortest
arc; long intentional rotations need intermediate waypoints.

The session waits at most 120 seconds for the prepared local singleplayer
spectator and matching first waypoint. It reads server state on the server
thread and requires disabled daylight/weather cycles; it makes no rule, time,
weather, block, entity or shader changes. These controls freeze daylight and
weather, **not** every simulation clock, mob, animation or shader history.
Actual world time/weather and Iris clocks remain in the evidence. Scene
preparation and any decision to freeze additional inputs belong to the runtime
owner.

After acquiring the UUID it holds the first pose for at least 30 seconds and
600 ticks (configurable up to 120 seconds). The owned player's delta movement
is cleared, position and rotation are set at normal Post ticks, and Minecraft's
previous-tick fields provide normal rendered interpolation. The initial snap
uses `setOldPosAndRot()` only before warmup. The moving path uses cubic easing
between waypoints with zero endpoint velocity and deterministic 20 Hz samples.
No OS input, direct mainCamera repositioning or render-frame teleport is used.

Capture scheduling uses path time and the observed render tick delta. Source
wall times are retained separately; slow ticks do not silently become a faster
path. Motion has a 60-second real-time bound. Server scene observations must
complete within five seconds after an owned scene starts. A changed UUID,
dimension, pause/menu, camera entity/type, shader fallback, loaded options,
render radius, framebuffer, control hash or tracked configuration fails the
session. Rain/thunder are required to remain settled during capture. Keep hands
off movement and mouse input during the owned run; source screenshots prove
the actual camera rather than assuming the planned camera was reached.

## Output and bounds

All outputs go to
`<gameDirectory>/camera-quality/<fresh-UUID>/`. Prepared game directories under
`run-workloads/` are already ignored. Do not run against a tracked game
directory or add these generated files to Git. The output root must not be a
symbolic link and resolves directly inside the game directory. Labels and
request content never become paths. Filenames are fixed `request.json`,
`manifest.json` and generated `frame-NNNN.png`; the manifest uses a sibling
temporary file followed by replacement.

The 24-second example requests 241 slots, including start and end; the maximum
is 301. OpenGL readback is on the render thread immediately after the frame's
GUI pass. PNG writing/hashing uses one daemon writer with **one in-flight
image**, no queue of native images. The framebuffer is bounded to 4096×2160
pixels (about 34 MiB of RGBA source pixels). Each PNG is limited to 64 MiB;
the sequence has a 2 GiB disk budget with capacity reserved before the next
capture. These are experiment bounds, not promises that readback/compression
is fast. Slower storage/readback may require using `fps: 5` or `fps: 2`.

If a render misses a scheduled slot or the writer is still busy, that slot is
retained as `missed_render_slot` or `writer_backpressure`. The harness never
duplicates a later screenshot to fill missing motion. PNG write completion
returns to the client thread and records hash, size, UTC completion and write
wall time. The final manifest waits for that callback, with a 30-second timeout;
the manifest is also checkpointed after every successful write callback.
an unresolved writer remains explicit in the failed report. A timeout can leave
the daemon writer finishing an owned file, but cannot be called completed
capture evidence.

Each captured checkpoint records actual rendered mainCamera position/yaw/pitch,
local player pose, motion tick/delta, planned/observed path seconds, actual
wall time, session render count, Iris source frame counter and frame-time
sources, the dev GPU frame ID, framebuffer size, world time/weather, actual
loaded pack, capture-boundary archive/options hashes and screenshot completion.
GPU frame IDs may stay zero if the existing GPU timer is disabled; they are not
a GPU measurement here. Full loaded shader options, mod versions, initial/start/
end input snapshots, class bytecode identity, exact request/config and advancing
shader temporal inputs are retained in the manifest. Archive hashes are checked
at initial/start/end boundaries; loaded options/config/control are checked each
second. Mid-frame pack reloads are not permitted and need separate coverage.

Statuses distinguish `rejected_request`, `failed`, `incomplete_capture` and
`complete`. A completed sequence requires every requested slot's successful
write callback. Rejected or partial attempts are retained, not erased. Without
`cameraQualityOnly`, the harness restores its acquired player's original pose
when that same UUID remains present. It never stops another process by name.

## Physical units, validation and transition semantics

Java defaults: near32, far96, transition8 blocks. Snapshot repairs far to at
least near+1 and clamps transition to min(2*near,far-near). LodSettings rejects
nonfinite values, near≤0, far≤near, negative or overlapping width. Shader input
must independently reject invalid values; do not silently clamp malformed
core bands into a different quality setting in this new consumer.

Use positive bounded checks matching existing Java ranges: 1≤near≤4095,
2≤far≤4096, far>near, 0≤transition≤512 and transition≤min(2*near,far-near).
The conjunction rejects NaN via false ordered comparisons and infinity via
finite bounds; it needs no GLSL120 isnan/isinf assumption. Every validation
input is a uniform. Unknown ordinal or invalid bands restores original normal
SSR before any distance classifier. Java-repaired raw config values are valid
transported values; an invalid TOML edit cannot be assumed to exercise an
invalid-uniform fallback. Negative uniform cases require source fixtures or a
separate controlled diagnostic, never unauthorized production-provider edits.

Distance is length(viewPos) from the original screen2view reconstruction, in
camera/view-space Minecraft blocks. Preserve feet/world coordinates only for
the pack's existing roughness behavior. Do not use feet length, abs(z), depth,
world origin or the reflected ray endpoint for the core zones.

Adopt the existing core/Photon centered-width convention locally, without
importing its shared helper or temporal random selector. With N=near, F=far,
W=transition, full→middle occupies [N-W/2,N+W/2], middle→far occupies
[F-W/2,F+W/2]. W is each band's total physical width, not a fraction, a whole
near-to-far interval or a refinement count. Valid width keeps bands nonoverlapping
and the near band's lower edge nonnegative. Example96/160/W8 gives92–100 and
156–164. The full near output is assured through the lower edge; the centered
near transition intentionally straddles the ideal N threshold. Do not describe
every pixel below N as untouched full-quality output when W>0.

W=0 has hard, deterministic thresholds: d<N uses full, N≤d<F middle, d≥F far.
W>0 uses smoothstep weights inside each band and one pure budget outside them.
Where adjacent budgets are equal (BALANCED near, AGGRESSIVE far), collapse to
one result/sample path. No temporal noise, frame dither, new roughness pattern
or unverified temporal accumulator is proposed. Smooth weights are mathematically
continuous; they do not guarantee stable moving hit geometry or accepted motion.

Transition-quality mode2 runs **one** original outer march and **one** fixed
four-step refinement chain on eligible hits, retaining the states after2/3/4.
Select one endpoint outside bands; inside a band evaluate at most the two
needed endpoint results from that same chain. No two complete SSR functions
execute. This diagnostic saves no refinement-depth fetches and can add a color
fetch in bands; it is a quality control, never performance evidence.

Blend endpoint results as reflected premultiplied contribution and opacity,
then reconstruct the unpremultiplied return only when opacity>0. That preserves
the existing caller's mix(base,reflection.rgb,reflection.a*reflectivity*factor).
Straight independent RGB/alpha interpolation can darken a valid-to-miss blend
because a miss returns zero RGBA; do not use it as a transition shortcut. At
pure weights return the selected endpoint directly. Preserve each endpoint's
original final depth guard/vignette/fresnel rather than sharing an approximate
acceptance result. Validate this algebra and edge cases before rendering.

Only after quality acceptance should savings mode3 bound the same single
refinement chain by the maximum of the actually needed endpoint counts (≤4).
Classify before refinement fetches; a hit-local policy may avoid classification
for misses/cutoff failures while always using the originating viewPos. A bounded
maximum-four loop/early exit or reviewed literal body is possible. Explicit
depth/color LOD0 accesses are mandatory in the active divergent budget path;
do not infer valid implicit derivatives from the baseline's existing branches.
Endpoint storage, extra color fetches, divisions, divergence and compiler/
register pressure may cancel any saved depth work. No gain is predicted.

With config mode nonzero and DEBUG_ALLOW1, exactversion2 shaderlodDebug!=0
selects the private diagnostic. Debug permission defaults0 and removes diagnostic
code from benchmark builds. Leave the permission fixed1 while testing live
debug false→true→false, then use permission0 for performance arms. Unknown
versions cannot interpret the debug field; they retain original normal output.

Eligible debug uses the same requested budget/transition policy: full/middle/
far colors green/yellow/red (consistent with current mod debug intent), with a
documented budget brightness legend4/3/2. Invalid preset/bands under known2 can
show a distinct error status; disabled under known2 can show yellow/status,
but debug-on images are intentionally diagnostic and do not assert normal
fallback image parity. Mode0 and debug-off fallbacks remain original. Existing
standalone cue can test absent-version status independently; do not add a new
production protocol field for that purpose.

The overlay is restricted to original qualifying reflection pixels and adds
no sampler. It must show requested policy, not claim an eligible hit/refinement
actually occurred. Reflection misses can display a requested far budget while
skipping refinement naturally. Debug must be off for normal quality/cost checks.
Palette changes prove value consumption at most; physical work needs separate
source/pass/counter and GPU evidence. Native color should return when debug is
cleared without a shader-option/source reload.

# Benchmark guide

For the local Asahi machine without a desktop, see [headless development](HEADLESS.md).
The maintained Linux ARM64 launcher selects its installed GPU-backed virtual
display when no display is explicitly selected; the native 2560×1600 viewport
and all normal benchmark guards remain required.

For the prepared RTX 2080 Ti Windows host, see [Windows benchmarking](WINDOWS_BENCHMARK.md).

Use the maintained command for discovery, planning, execution and results:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py discover
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py baseline --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --output FRESH_BASELINE
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py plan --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py check --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_CHECK_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py report --output REPORT
```

`discover` lists local managed slots, worlds and shader archives. It is an inventory, not compatibility approval. Use `--profile` instead of `--slot` for an explicit prepared client. Set `--width` and `--height` to the intended native viewport (the local Asahi fullscreen mode is 2560×1600). Select the exact original pack/options for the feature; private candidates use `--candidate` instead of `--feature`. See the [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md) for specialized scenes, compatibility checks and qualification protocols.

`baseline` renders the original pack with the main mod absent in the backed-up
authored save. After 120 seconds conditioning it captures three unchanged
20-second native windows, with the standard ownership, readiness, sample and
restoration checks. The report gives frame sample variance/SD (ms²/ms), and
separately variance/SD of the three window means and first-to-last drift.
These describe frame jitter and within-process variation, respectively; neither
is a confidence interval. Repeat in fresh processes to measure between-run
variation. Keep absent-mod baselines separate from the matched Master-Off
controls in optimization comparisons. Startup failure supplies no frame-time
measurement. `native-startup` remains a short original-only startup diagnostic.

`--gl-context native` preserves Minecraft's normal context request. For explicit
desktop API coverage, maintained comparisons also accept `3.2`, `4.3`, `4.5` and
`4.6`. These request real GLFW contexts; they do not override reported versions
or capabilities. Explicit requests disable NeoForge's reusable early window in
the owned profile, with the normal configuration backup/CAS/restoration contract.
The returned desktop version must meet the requested minimum and is recorded in
`summary.json.gl_context`. A driver returning4.6 for a4.5 request is labeled4.6;
it does not supply an independent4.5 result. Keep actual context/configuration
cohorts and their native baselines separate. Frozen Bliss qualification retains
its existing native-context protocol and refuses an explicit context override.
`--expected-renderer 'RTX 5080'` additionally refuses a ready client on a different
GPU, including a hardware integrated GPU. It validates the observed renderer
before scoring; it does not select the GPU or change personal driver settings.

`--performance-stack optimized` selects the exact pinned ModernFix, FerriteCore
and ImmediatelyFast tuple for G03 and its matched original-only startup/baselines or byte-identical native controls.
Default remains `minimal`. Other private/frozen protocols reject this override.
Preflight verifies every optional JAR, launch uses the maintained stack selector,
and runtime readiness checks the actual loaded module versions before scoring.
Optional artifacts are frozen operation inputs. Keep stack cohorts separate;
selecting the tuple is not proof that G03 compiled, executed, or helped.

`plan` runs the standard test's static checks without compiling, launching or creating the report. It lists the resolved launch plan, schedule, per-check elapsed time, failures and remedies. A stale build is reported; `test` rebuilds it automatically before launch. Native options and canonical profile inputs are checked; preserve unexplained differences before resetting a managed slot. Runtime-only checks still run in the client.

`check` accepts the same candidate arguments and exercises activation, available source/work checks, short captures and restoration without the two-minute conditioning period. It reports no performance or visual qualification. Use it when checking whether a newly integrated candidate runs; use `test` for a development performance comparison. Frozen Bliss qualification cannot use `check`.

`test` uses the fixed native/candidate/native-return protocol described below. `report` reads existing reports without launching anything, including historical reports. Its decision gives drift comparison precedence over an averaged positive mean, and identifies invalid runs or recovery requirements. It does not grant optimization closure or compatibility qualification. Phase timings in `summary.json` include nested profile preparation/restoration details; do not sum nested details into the total again.

Windows ownership JSON reads and atomic publication retry transient sharing errors
for at most three seconds, including CRT EACCES/EPERM errors that lack a Windows
error number; persistent denial still fails the operation. Normal
configuration restoration includes the five numbered FML backups for each
ShaderLOD client config. For an older interrupted report that omitted these
paths, `recover --output REPORT --preserve-generated-backups` retains newly
created known backups in that report before checking the complete original
profile map. Existing backups and unknown files retain normal ownership checks;
recovery never replays measurements.

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test \
  --profile /path/to/prepared/client \
  --pack /path/to/original-pack.zip \
  --pack-options /path/to/original-pack.zip.txt \
  --feature PUBLIC_OPTIMIZATION_ID \
  --output /path/to/fresh/report
```

The command automatically selects the existing Linux ARM64 launcher on that platform. Explicit `linux_arm64_runtime.py` commands remain supported. It finds an installed full JDK21 or a cached Gradle JDK21; an explicit JAVA_HOME retains precedence. Select an existing loader/version/scene slot; keep the report outside that slot and on the same filesystem as the profile. Confirm the lane is free and the inputs match the intended tuple before launch. Do not reset a slot owned by a client or interrupted operation. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout --help` describes managed checkout. Use `run_storage.copytree` for profile/world copies; it enforces storage limits.

The standard test targets the prepared NeoForge 1.21.1 benchmark protocol. It renders native Off for 120 seconds before measurement, then acquires native Off, singleton candidate through normal Apply, then native Off return: 20 seconds each, with separate warmup, startup and recovery within a 900-second budget. Conditioning was added after repeated first-to-return drift; it does not prove stability. It records total-frame timing, drift, stills and restoration in the report. A valid slower result is still a result; a failed or invalid run is not a speed conclusion. Inspect `summary.json`, errors and restoration before proceeding. A short result is not proof of visual equivalence, DH/PBR compatibility or final closure. Compare matched total-frame measurements and disclose drift and scope.

C02 is an explicitly labeled 2×2 bloom quality tradeoff, with Master-On native
controls; its scoped exception is documented in the [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md#c02-experimental-bloom-shading-rate).

## Choose the check for the question

| Question | Maintained route | What it does not establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What inputs and candidates exist? | `discover`, then `plan` with selected inputs | Runtime compatibility or ownership |
| Does this change activate and recover? | `check` | Performance or visual equivalence |
| Is the idea worth more investigation? | `test`, then `report` | Broad workload/machine qualification |
| What does native do without ShaderLOD? | `baseline` | Installed-Off overhead by itself |
| Does it preserve motion or work across packs/hardware? | Candidate-specific protocols in the reference | Coverage of untested scenes, transitions or machines |

Before designing a new study, establish the user's intended decision: deep
workload performance, compatibility breadth, quality, or a quick screen. Reuse
the supported commands above. Put the chosen claim, comparator, coverage, useful
metrics, controls and budget in the existing experiment record. Record exclusions
and fallback separately; do not impose a universal repetition count or payback
horizon. Performance requires actual-window execution and valid output evidence,
not merely enabling a setting. Source changes do not inherit earlier timings.

## What caused the gap between less shader work and no FPS gain

Two observed CPU mechanisms were substantial: repeated source validation on
active render paths, and validation/resource observation on Photon's inactive
history path. Compile/link receipts move immutable input verification away from
draws while retaining live ownership, option, sampler and restoration checks.
Photon's inactive repair supplies direct before/after runtime evidence; removing
source calls on AO establishes CPU work removal without establishing an AO win.

Depth replay and half-resolution AO also add work: geometry submissions,
producer targets, binding checks and reconstruction. Current MakeUp/Unbound
depth clocks show increased render CPU and total-frame time. Half-AO permission
counts show valid producer execution, not how many pixels avoid native AO:
fallback/partial-confidence paths can retain the original kernel as well as new
producer/reconstruction costs. Exact per-component allocation remains unproved.

GPU reductions are conditional. Far shadow, visible clouds, water and full-
confidence AO each have different eligible coverage. Native compilation may
already remove some dead work; explicit/implicit sampling and dynamic loops
can affect code generation. Those are hypotheses where not isolated by an A/B
experiment. Source tap counts are not issued hardware-instruction counts.

# Benchmark guide

For the local Asahi machine without a desktop, see [headless development](HEADLESS.md).
The maintained Linux ARM64 launcher selects its installed GPU-backed virtual
display when no display is explicitly selected; the native 2560×1600 viewport
and all normal benchmark guards remain required.

For the prepared RTX 2080 Ti Windows host, see [Windows benchmarking](WINDOWS_BENCHMARK.md).

Use the maintained command for discovery, planning, execution and results:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py discover
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py baseline --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --output FRESH_BASELINE
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py plan --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py check --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_CHECK_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py report --output REPORT
```

`discover` lists local managed slots, worlds and shader archives. It is an inventory, not compatibility approval. Use `--profile` instead of `--slot` for an explicit prepared client. Set `--width` and `--height` to the intended native viewport (the local Asahi fullscreen mode is 2560×1600). Select the exact original pack/options for the feature; private candidates use `--candidate` instead of `--feature`. See the [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md) for specialized scenes, compatibility checks and qualification protocols.

`baseline` renders the original pack with the main mod absent in the backed-up
authored save. After 120 seconds conditioning it captures three unchanged
20-second native windows, with the standard ownership, readiness, sample and
restoration checks. The report gives frame sample variance/SD (ms²/ms), and
separately variance/SD of the three window means and first-to-last drift.
These describe frame jitter and within-process variation, respectively; neither
is a confidence interval. Repeat in fresh processes to measure between-run
variation. Keep absent-mod baselines separate from the matched Master-Off
controls in optimization comparisons. Startup failure supplies no frame-time
measurement. `native-startup` remains a short original-only startup diagnostic.

`--gl-context native` preserves Minecraft's normal context request. For explicit
desktop API coverage, maintained comparisons also accept `3.2`, `4.3`, `4.5` and
`4.6`. These request real GLFW contexts; they do not override reported versions
or capabilities. Explicit requests disable NeoForge's reusable early window in
the owned profile, with the normal configuration backup/CAS/restoration contract.
The returned desktop version must meet the requested minimum and is recorded in
`summary.json.gl_context`. A driver returning4.6 for a4.5 request is labeled4.6;
it does not supply an independent4.5 result. Keep actual context/configuration
cohorts and their native baselines separate. Frozen Bliss qualification retains
its existing native-context protocol and refuses an explicit context override.
`--expected-renderer 'RTX 5080'` additionally refuses a ready client on a different
GPU, including a hardware integrated GPU. It validates the observed renderer
before scoring; it does not select the GPU or change personal driver settings.

`plan` runs the standard test's static checks without compiling, launching or creating the report. It lists the resolved launch plan, schedule, per-check elapsed time, failures and remedies. A stale build is reported; `test` rebuilds it automatically before launch. Native options and canonical profile inputs are checked; preserve unexplained differences before resetting a managed slot. Runtime-only checks still run in the client.

`check` accepts the same candidate arguments and exercises activation, available source/work checks, short captures and restoration without the two-minute conditioning period. It reports no performance or visual qualification. Use it when checking whether a newly integrated candidate runs; use `test` for a development performance comparison. Frozen Bliss qualification cannot use `check`.

`test` uses the fixed native/candidate/native-return protocol described below. `report` reads existing reports without launching anything, including historical reports. Its decision gives drift comparison precedence over an averaged positive mean, and identifies invalid runs or recovery requirements. It does not grant optimization closure or compatibility qualification. Phase timings in `summary.json` include nested profile preparation/restoration details; do not sum nested details into the total again.

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

| --- | --- | --- |

Before designing a new study, establish the user's intended decision: deep

## Opened producer, consumer and native-work contracts

**P — Photon.** [Vertex](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r5/shadow-producer/sources/photon/shaders/program/shadow.vsh:84)
updates optional voxels at 89–91 **before** Nether clipping at 93–97; animation at
103–119 precedes quartic-norm distortion. [Fragment](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r5/shadow-producer/sources/photon/shaders/program/shadow.fsh:106)
water uses a refracted procedural normal, old/new derivative-area ratio and a
five-metre absorption path; nonwater samples atlas LOD0, discards alpha < 0.1 and
writes colored transmission. This is not an immutable block-depth producer.
`settings.glsl:17–21` defaults to 2048, 128 m, interval 2 and hardware filtering
for depth1; actual pixel size multiplies `MC_SHADOW_QUALITY`
(`pcss.glsl:26`). Shadow color clear is zero; alpha test/blend are explicitly off
in properties because the shader implements its own discard.

All direct depth/color sampling source groups are `pcss.glsl`, Overworld/End/water
volumetric fog, and final's debug/activation read. Their literal callers cover
`deferred4`, forward translucent/particle/water wrappers including DH water, and
`composite` fog. `c1_blend_layers` declares samplers but a declaration alone is not
a live read. `shadow_basic` also reads a 3×3 color neighbourhood; PCSS has
raw-depth blocker/SSS statistics, **separate biased opaque and translucent
coordinates**, four initial color/depth samples, and native four-probe early
exits (`pcss.glsl:29–87,117–183,195–281`). Water fog uses raw depth distance in
absorption (`water_fog_vl.glsl:87–113`), so a binary visibility replacement loses
more than a shadow intensity. Optional voxel producer/propagation is a separate
output transaction and cannot be dropped when visible shadows are absent.

**C-R / C-U — Complementary.** Both original archives' shadow program is read
independently by the reproducer; shared source is one family, not two transfers.
[Shadow](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r5/shadow-producer/sources/complementary-reimagined/shaders/program/shadow.glsl:52)
uses atlas LOD0, dithered entity fade, connected glass, water caustic textures and
separate animated underwater shaft noise. It writes `shadowcolor0` and, for
quality ≥ 1, `shadowcolor1`; the latter alpha encodes caster height
`0.25 + max(0, positionYM*0.05)` (219–224), with explicit glass/water adjustments.
Vertex work includes waving, light/time-dependent foliage adjustment, camera
distance-dependent water displacement, and optional light/puddle/reflection
voxel and player-vertex writes (304–344). Radial distortion is
`d = r*b + 1-b`, `b=1-25.6/shadowDistance`, with depth ×0.2; source default
distance 192 m and quality-dependent map size 1024/2048/4096 (`common:494–502`).

All direct sampling groups are `shadowSampling`, volumetric light, `mainClouds`
and the Nether activation read in `gbuffers_basic`. Lighting includes reach
terrain/entities/hand/water/translucent and DH wrappers; volumetric light also
appears through reflection/water paths; clouds feed deferred and water/reflection
paths. `worldSpaceRef` is an additional indirect lighting/reflection consumer,
not a new standalone depth sampler. The scene-aware shaft branch reads both
raw depth0 and **shadowcolor1 alpha** (`volumetricLight:304–306`); colored shafts

## Complete producerEpoch and transaction contract

The existing [ShadowTraversalEpochs](../SHADOW_TRAVERSAL_EPOCHS_R1.md) tracks CPU
manager structure, task and lifetime; its five immutable coverage gaps still
refuse reuse. Equal traversal epochs do **not** certify unchanged shadow outputs.
No change to that model is made here. A future B1 producerEpoch must separately
bind all of the following to the actual completed producer generation:

- Exact pack/member/preprocessed source, loaded options, renderer/version and
  world/pipeline identities; shadow programs/fallbacks, participating caster
  classes, DH/Colorwheel/Voxy paths and resource-pack/model/material versions.
- Current shadow model/projection/light transforms, distortion and depth scale,
  camera-relative origin/snapping, map dimensions and MC shadow quality,
  viewport/scissor, bias/cull/depth/alpha/blend states and clear policy.
- Geometry/list/upload/arena lifetime, entity pose and skin, block entities,
  atlas pixels and animated atlas frame, shader waving/caustic/dither time,
  rain/wetness/biome/lightmap and every other consumed producer uniform.
- Depth0/depth1 opaque/translucent ordering and content generation, color0/1
  contents/formats, physical texture/flip identities, border/filter/compare/mip
  state, and voxel/puddle/reflection/player-list outputs and their consumers.
- Complete dirty **old and new** caster footprints expanded by raster coverage,
  all downstream filter/blocker supports and any derivative neighbourhood.
  Exposed tiles after camera/sun/map changes must be repaired; local content
  equality cannot be inferred from unchanged chunk geometry or texture IDs.

A cache miss performs the complete native transaction. A cache hit must preserve
side effects or separately prove their equivalent execution, then merge both
depth layers and their corresponding color outputs using native ownership,
ordering and blend semantics. Copying only the minimum scalar depth is not that
merge. Query/build/copy/merge/clear/dirty-tracking/extra submission costs count;
plain cadence intentionally omits required updates and remains a closed premise.

B2 demand must be available **before** shadow production and be the union of
opaque, translucent, particle, water/reflection, fog/cloud, DH and side-effect
support. Reprojected old depth is not a conservative current demand mask through
disocclusion. An off-camera 10 m tree under light elevation 10° can cast a shadow
about 56.7 m into visible terrain. Camera occlusion and camera-distance footprint
therefore cannot reject its light-space support. The native distortion itself
already concentrates texels near the camera; B3 must compare against that map.
For radial `r/(br+1-b)`, tangential scale is `1/(br+1-b)` and radial scale is
`(1-b)/(br+1-b)^2`; one scalar radius is not an isotropic footprint. Photon uses a
different quartic metric and Sildur/Bliss logarithmic maps.

B3 accounting must include sum of cascade caster submissions/vertices, duplicate
alpha-tested coverage, clears/color maps, cascade lookup/blending, expanded
transition/filter guards and voxel side-effect ownership. Two 1024² cascades
have half a 2048² map's nominal texels but can execute a shared caster twice;
that does not prove less shader work. A matrix replacement must update **every**
consumer above, including raw-depth fog and blocker distance reconstruction.

## Portable scalar B4 opportunity and cost falsifier

A full RG32F min/max pyramid at 2048² contains 5,592,405 texels: **44,739,240 B**
(42.67 MiB) for one depth domain before ping-pong/other maps. That is not the
minimum construction. Starting reduction at 1024² needs 11,184,808 B; a fixed
4×4 **minimum-only** tile field needs 512² scalars (1,048,576 useful R32F bytes).
This is a fresh, narrower B4 premise, not a retry of the receiver A4 plateau.

The best opened scope is BSL's ordinary nine-position radius-one receiver with
subsurface=0: include all bilinear-compare support texels, query at most four
4×4 tile minima and return native white **only if every relevant depth0 sample
is certainly lit**. Native colored work is then skipped by its own branch;
otherwise run the untouched receiver. Do not synthesize black from depth0.
Leave SSS, shafts, fog, unknown borders and different radii native. This needs
correct comparison mode and a conservative rounding margin; scalar arithmetic
alone does not certify actual depth conversion/driver filtering. A rectangular
superset may lower hit rate but must never miss a supporting texel. The four-tile
count assumes actual physical depth extent equals the source-declared map size:
native offset is `1/shadowMapResolution`, not automatically one physical texel.
At physical/declared ratio 2, its six-texel-wide bilinear support can cross three
4×4 tiles on each axis. Bind both dimensions/MC quality before choosing the
query count. The scalar tests include this counterexample.

Two further gates from the independent remaining-shader challenge remain open.
The min producer must obtain **raw noncomparison depth** while native BSL uses
`sampler2DShadow` and actual hardware comparison. Merely declaring sampler2D over
the same image does not prove a valid raw-sampling route; the exact Iris alias/
sampler binding and actual state must be joined. Also, the fallback color fetch
uses implicit derivatives. An all-lit early-return lane beside a colored dark
lane can change helper/derivative behavior. Preserve or prove original-equivalent
color LOD and helper execution across such quads; scalar visibility equivalence
does not certify the compiled fallback. The original also contains conditional
color sampling, which does not establish equivalence after adding another branch.

Fresh exact-Iris binary inspection finds an actual graphics `ShadowCompositeRenderer`
path: `ProgramSource` → program/FBO/viewport → fullscreen quad, followed by
ordinary rendering; this is **not compute-only**. [Pipeline disassembly](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r5/shadow-producer/iris-shadow-pipeline.javap.txt)
and [shadow renderer/targets](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r5/shadow-producer/iris-shadow-targets.javap.txt)
are from JAR SHA `3e3f94d2d5cdcb8145c4385d521974aa2d8669b2cc212351f70cf06488182e83`.
`IrisRenderingPipeline.renderShadows` calls ShadowRenderer then prepare;
ShadowRenderer invokes the shadow composite renderer. Thus a fragment/FBO path
is source-feasible on this renderer without adding compute/SSBO/imageStore.

**Resource caveat:** the inspected ShadowRenderTargets allocation takes the
full shadow resolution for both dimensions. A quarter viewport does not make a
512² allocation. A spare BSL shadowcolor1 is only a source hypothesis and would
need an actual format/flip/sampler/clear certificate; an R32F 2048² target costs
16,777,216 B per physical image, not 1 MiB. Extra simultaneous samplers, hidden
alternate allocation and DH/PBR must fit actual limits. No resource is assigned
or pack patched here.

Let F be output pixels, R eligible ordinary-receiver **invocations**, p=R/F their
invocation density, and h the certificate hit fraction over those invocations.
Forward overdraw/material/translucent layers can make p greater than 1; screen
pixel coverage is not a measurement of R. A simplistic **fetch-expression** model
for a 4×4 reduction counts N² build fetches, ≤4 proof fetches per eligible invocation,
then 9 native fetches on misses. To beat nine native expressions requires
`9 h > 4 + N²/(p F)`, before writes/branches/FBO/clear/derivative overhead.
For N=2048, F=1920×1200, p=1 needs h>0.647; p=0.5 needs h>0.849;
p<0.364 cannot win even at h=1 under this simplified model, where p is actual
invocation density, not the fraction of visible screen pixels. Hardware PCF
expressions and raw fetches are **not equal-cost operations**, so this is an
investment screen, not a speed prediction. Caching the tile field reintroduces
the complete B1 producerEpoch problem. Raw-access sampler/setup, 16 source
fetches per useful tile, full-target clear/alternate-image traffic and
helper/fallback execution must all be counted. A hierarchy shared with another consumer
needs demonstrated compatible support and cannot double-count A4 savings.

The next cheap predicate is a bounded original-input scalar query of these exact
supports and h/p counts under original BSL options; if the optimistic expression
screen fails, do not build the extra pass. If it passes, root can decide whether
one private shader/native-control pair and actual resource/branch qualification
is worth creating. Such a snapshot must include current depth0 values and the
actual reached receiver coordinates/bias, invocation multiplicity and physical
depth extent; screenshots or source-defined N alone cannot supply h. No such
snapshot or runtime result exists in this handback.

B5 does not replace these predicates. Equal first two depth moments can encode
different visibility (the scalar test uses distributions over 0, 1/3, 2/3, 1
with counts `[1,3,3,1]` versus `[0,6,0,2]`; both mean 1/2 and second moment 1/3,
but lit fractions at reference 1/2 differ 1/2 versus 1/4). Colored transmission,
raw-depth absorption and blocker/SSS statistics require additional retained
resources. Filtering/reduction/bias/bleeding fixes and receiver changes count
against saved PCF; short native kernels offer no automatic amortization.

# Benchmark guide

For the local Asahi machine without a desktop, see [headless development](HEADLESS.md).
The maintained Linux ARM64 launcher selects its installed GPU-backed virtual
display when no display is explicitly selected; the native 2560×1600 viewport
and all normal benchmark guards remain required.

For the prepared RTX 2080 Ti Windows host, see [Windows benchmarking](WINDOWS_BENCHMARK.md).

Use the maintained command for discovery, planning, execution and results:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py discover
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py baseline --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --output FRESH_BASELINE
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py plan --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py check --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_CHECK_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py report --output REPORT
```

`discover` lists local managed slots, worlds and shader archives. It is an inventory, not compatibility approval. Use `--profile` instead of `--slot` for an explicit prepared client. Set `--width` and `--height` to the intended native viewport (the local Asahi fullscreen mode is 2560×1600). Select the exact original pack/options for the feature; private candidates use `--candidate` instead of `--feature`. See the [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md) for specialized scenes, compatibility checks and qualification protocols.

`baseline` renders the original pack with the main mod absent in the backed-up
authored save. After 120 seconds conditioning it captures three unchanged
20-second native windows, with the standard ownership, readiness, sample and
restoration checks. The report gives frame sample variance/SD (ms²/ms), and
separately variance/SD of the three window means and first-to-last drift.
These describe frame jitter and within-process variation, respectively; neither
is a confidence interval. Repeat in fresh processes to measure between-run
variation. Keep absent-mod baselines separate from the matched Master-Off
controls in optimization comparisons. Startup failure supplies no frame-time
measurement. `native-startup` remains a short original-only startup diagnostic.

`--gl-context native` preserves Minecraft's normal context request. For explicit
desktop API coverage, maintained comparisons also accept `3.2`, `4.3`, `4.5` and
`4.6`. These request real GLFW contexts; they do not override reported versions
or capabilities. Explicit requests disable NeoForge's reusable early window in
the owned profile, with the normal configuration backup/CAS/restoration contract.
The returned desktop version must meet the requested minimum and is recorded in
`summary.json.gl_context`. A driver returning4.6 for a4.5 request is labeled4.6;
it does not supply an independent4.5 result. Keep actual context/configuration
cohorts and their native baselines separate. Frozen Bliss qualification retains
its existing native-context protocol and refuses an explicit context override.
`--expected-renderer 'RTX 5080'` additionally refuses a ready client on a different
GPU, including a hardware integrated GPU. It validates the observed renderer
before scoring; it does not select the GPU or change personal driver settings.

`--performance-stack optimized` selects the exact pinned ModernFix, FerriteCore
and ImmediatelyFast tuple for G03 and its matched original-only startup/baselines or byte-identical native controls.
Default remains `minimal`. Other private/frozen protocols reject this override.
Preflight verifies every optional JAR, launch uses the maintained stack selector,
and runtime readiness checks the actual loaded module versions before scoring.
Optional artifacts are frozen operation inputs. Keep stack cohorts separate;
selecting the tuple is not proof that G03 compiled, executed, or helped.

`plan` runs the standard test's static checks without compiling, launching or creating the report. It lists the resolved launch plan, schedule, per-check elapsed time, failures and remedies. A stale build is reported; `test` rebuilds it automatically before launch. Native options and canonical profile inputs are checked; preserve unexplained differences before resetting a managed slot. Runtime-only checks still run in the client.

`check` accepts the same candidate arguments and exercises activation, available source/work checks, short captures and restoration without the two-minute conditioning period. It reports no performance or visual qualification. Use it when checking whether a newly integrated candidate runs; use `test` for a development performance comparison. Frozen Bliss qualification cannot use `check`.

`test` uses the fixed native/candidate/native-return protocol described below. `report` reads existing reports without launching anything, including historical reports. Its decision gives drift comparison precedence over an averaged positive mean, and identifies invalid runs or recovery requirements. It does not grant optimization closure or compatibility qualification. Phase timings in `summary.json` include nested profile preparation/restoration details; do not sum nested details into the total again.

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

```sh

It finds an installed full JDK21 or a cached Gradle JDK21; an explicit JAVA_HOME retains precedence. Select an existing loader/version/scene slot; keep the report outside that slot and on the same filesystem as the profile. Confirm the lane is free and the inputs match the intended tuple before launch. Do not reset a slot owned by a client or interrupted operation. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout --help` describes managed checkout. Use `run_storage.copytree` for profile/world copies; it enforces storage limits.

The standard test targets the prepared NeoForge 1.21.1 benchmark protocol. Conditioning was added after repeated first-to-return drift; it does not prove stability. It records total-frame timing, drift, stills and restoration in the report. A valid slower result is still a result; a failed or invalid run is not a speed conclusion. Inspect `summary.json`, errors and restoration before proceeding. A short result is not proof of visual equivalence, DH/PBR compatibility or final closure. Compare matched total-frame measurements and disclose drift and scope.

## Decisive native path

Pinned **BSL 10.1.8**, original archive SHA-256
`36b0a50ff7918bf10e9422c401d93779f9d0088a26acea975b435243f96930b5`.
Entry is `shaders/world0/gbuffers_terrain.fsh` →
`program/gbuffers_terrain.glsl` → `lib/lighting/forwardLighting.glsl:GetLighting`
→ `lib/lighting/shadows.glsl:GetShadow`.

`GetShadow` computes native projected raw shadow coordinates and sets
`shadowFade = clamp(100 - 100 * max(abs(rawShadowPos.x), abs(rawShadowPos.y)), 0, 1)`.
Overworld additionally multiplies its native skylight fade. At
`shadowFade < 0.00001` it **already returns full light before the receiver bias,
SampleFilteredShadow or SampleBasicShadow call**. Exact fade0 is inside that
existing native predicate. The nine mandatory comparisons and up to nine
conditional depth/color pairs in the filtered helper are therefore already
excluded by source control flow at the proposed endpoint. A second exact-zero
branch cannot remove them again.

This fade is a **dimensionless projected shadow-map extent**, not a camera
radius in blocks. Its spatial ramp spans raw extent0.99 to1.0. The separate
DH branch uses `length(worldPos)`/`far` in blocks and existing native dither or
fade; DH is absent in the historical actual original scope used here. No new
threshold, projected metric, interpolation policy or block-distance setting
is introduced. The existing near-zero return is upstream behavior, not a
proposal to widen an exact-zero test.

## Equation and invariants

Let b be coarse noise, d interpolated detail noise, c native height coverage,
s sun coverage, A cloud amount, and w=`.0476*CLOUD_DETAIL`. In clear weather the
native pre-clamp expression is

```text
y = 21*mix(b,d,w) - c - (3*s+A)
density = CloudApplyDensity(max(y,0))
U = 21*mix(b,1,w) - c - (3*s+A)
```

The pinned normalized noise and linear sampling put d in[0,1]. All five native
detail settings put w in[.01428,.08092]. Thus y≤U in real arithmetic. The
candidate substitutes density0 only when its bounded finite-domain checks pass
and U<−.001. Equality and ambiguous near-zero values retain both detail reads.
This is a zero-density certificate, not a small-contribution threshold.
Native density scaling and division by `sqrt(q*q+.5)` preserve q=0.

The actual shader retains the native ordered expression. The .001 negative gap
is large relative to the observed binary32 lowering differences, but the finite
CPU checks are not a universal GLSL precision proof. The source keeps ordered
base/gradient/sun/coverage and finite-coordinate guards. Clear eligibility is
the uniform `rainStrength==0` condition, selected before any runtime result;
other weather enters the native function before classification.

Every caller update still executes with that zero density: sample lighting,
distance fade, cloud opacity, softened opacity, first-cloud/cloudViewLength and
final feedback. There is no loop continue, changed stride, alpha rescaling,
shifted dither or temporal modification. Reflections, skybox, other dimensions,
DH/Voxy and the advanced-material shader mode take their original sampling
paths. Other PBR resource combinations still need compatibility evidence.

Retained detail lookups use explicit LOD0. An early return followed by implicit
texture reads would introduce an undefined-derivative boundary. The native
wrapper already enables the ARB texture-LOD extension. Historical actual BSL
readback showed RGBA8, level0, isotropic nonmip LINEAR sampling; the pinned

## Work reduction and overhead

For K reached eligible samples, R successful zero certificates and F finite-domain
fallbacks after the initial base read, nominal lookup counts are

```text
native:     3K
candidate:  3K - 2R + F
```

Each certificate removes both detail lookups and the remaining native density
combination at that sample. A domain fallback can replay the native base read;
the F term charges that extra work. Runtime R/K and F are unknown. Source lookup
counts do not establish hardware transactions: filtering, caches, compiler
flattening and partially occupied execution groups can alter the saving.

The authentic512² noise image contains262,144 texels. At texel centers with
native detail1/amount10, clear weather and sunCoverage0, the independent census
found the following headroom:

| Height fraction | Certified texels | Fraction | Nominal three-read reduction, F=0 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| .125 | 93,788 |35.78%|23.85%|
| .5 |131,303|50.09%|33.39%|
| .75 |194,574|74.22%|49.48%|

These are texture envelopes, not reached-ray, bilinear or screen-pixel coverage.
The candidate adds dependent arithmetic/comparisons between base and detail,

It can reduce texture overlap or lose savings through divergent quad execution.
The nonclear path still pays the outer decision. If f is the unknown original
frame-time share of these noise queries, ideal total saving is at most roughly
`f*(2R-F)/(3K)` before those costs. No measured f or FPS percentage is available.

## Parent integration API

At the actual shadow-only `createTerrainRenderList` boundary:

```java
var capture = ShadowTraversalTouches.begin(managerIdentity, frame);
// Run the full original traversal unchanged.
var snapshot = ShadowTraversalTouches.finish(capture);

```

The parent must arrange reliable exception cleanup and must not begin a scope
for the main traversal. `begin(owner, frame, maxSections, maxWrites)` allows
smaller bounds. Maximum bounds are 65,536 identities and 1,048,576 writes;
zero/negative/larger requested limits yield an incomplete inactive token.
`begin` additionally requires explicit true for
`shaderlod.dev.shadowTraversalCertificate`; default Off opens no scope.
The setter hooks check `isCapturing()` before native getters or recording.
Property eligibility is checked at begin; an already opened diagnostic scope
continues until finish/abort. This is a scope gate, not a reuse toggle.

Scopes are `ThreadLocal`, with synchronized token accesses for misuse detection.
Nested begin invalidates both tokens and retains the outer active scope. Finishing
the rejected nested token leaves the outer scope alone. Wrong-thread finish
invalidates its token without clearing the owner thread's context; foreign-thread
setter writes without a local scope are ignored. The caller must still close the
owner scope. Finish releases mutable identity/order storage; snapshots retain
their bounded immutable entry copies and opaque identities. Abort and repeated
finish cannot produce a complete result. Unknown identities/writers, foreign-frame
stamp writes, disposal and section/write overflow produce incomplete diagnostics.
Write count saturates at the configured limit; an overflow receipt does not claim
to retain/count every subsequent write.

## Exact reserved obligations and allocation ordering

Actual `IrisSamplers` static initializer sets WORLD `{0,1,2}`, SODIUM `{0,2}`,
COMPOSITE **`{1,2}`**. `addLevelSamplers` identifies these external obligations:
unit 0 = `tex/texture/gtexture`; unit 1 = `iris_overlay`; unit 2 = `lightmap`.
Those world/Sodium paths must retain their externally managed bindings.

Actual `CompositeRenderer.createProgram` passes COMPOSITE to
`ProgramBuilder.begin` at bytecode 138–141. ProgramBuilder links before creating
ProgramSamplers. Its Builder subtracts the entire reserved-set size, even when
there is no linked external sampler. It skips reserved indices during allocation.
On the project's stated 16-fragment-unit Apple limit, this leaves 14 dynamic
bindings. A future runtime diagnostic must record the actual 34930 query value;
these original failure logs do not themselves retain that integer.

The complete composite creation method registers the following, in order:

| Composite bytecode | Registration / obligation |
| --- | --- |
| 221 | `addRenderTargetSamplers`: ascending RT index, grouped modern/legacy aliases; then `dhDepthTex/dhDepthTex0` together and distinct `dhDepthTex1` |
| 230 | Iris custom textures |
| 239 | Custom-image texture samplers |
| 272 | `noisetex` |
| 281 | `gdepthtex/depthtex0` together, `depthtex1`, `depthtex2` |
| 317 | Shadow depth/color/hardware-filter samplers, if linked shadow names exist |
| 367 | `iris_centerDepthSmooth`, if linked |

Image bindings separately registered at 254/263 are not sampler units. There is
**no `addLevelSamplers` or `addExternalSampler` call in this method**. Thus the
two composite reservations have no registered overlay/lightmap obligation here.
`FullScreenQuadRenderer.begin/renderQuad/end` bind/draw the vertex buffer and
change depth/polygon state; they do not rebind overlay/lightmap textures.
`CompositeRenderer.renderAll` uses the program at 369, draws at 409, clears
sampler listeners/objects at 443 and clears cached texture bindings across the
native-unit range at 450–491. Any experimental correction must preserve this
cleanup and the next world program's ordinary binding updates.

Builder `addDynamicSampler` only allocates when a requested uniform location
is not -1. All names in one registration share one unit; its remaining counter
decrements **once per successful registration**, not once per alias. It does not
deduplicate separate registrations. `addDefaultSampler` can reserve unit 0 even
without an active named uniform for default-zero sampler semantics. Consequently
the allocation count is a binding-group count, not automatically a count of all
active sampler uniforms.
