# Shared spatial evaluation and reconstruction kernel

2026-10-05. ShaderLOD original MIT mechanism:
[`spatial_pipeline.glsl`](../shaderpacks/common/shaders/include/shaderlod/spatial_pipeline.glsl).
It implements fixed screen tiles, all-member receiver classification, current-frame
cache handling and linear reconstruction. It contains no Photon algorithm,
material decoder, sampler, implicit derivative, uniform, temporal reuse or source
rewriter. Existing Photon sources/archives, Java and work/volume helpers are unchanged.
This is a bounded adapter handoff, not another supported pack or production pass graph.

Include `work_policy.glsl`, `spatial_plan.glsl` and
`surface_region_continuity.glsl` before `spatial_pipeline.glsl`. Copy those explicit
common files into an adapter's reviewed include tree, preserve MIT attribution and
record their hashes. Repeated guards use `#if !defined` rather than declaring Iris
boolean options. The [spatial planner](SPATIAL_LOD_PLAN.md) supplies distance
tier weights; the [region guard](SURFACE_REGION_CONTINUITY.md) supplies the existing
sampler-free geometry/material predicate. Its thresholds and optional lighting
spread remain heuristics; neither cache metadata nor this pipeline establishes a
bound on missed thin cast shadows.

## Adapter callbacks and declared quantity

The complete callback declarations are in the kernel:

```glsl
ShaderlodSpatialSurface shaderlod_spatial_adapter_surface(ivec2 pixel);
ShaderlodSpatialSpread shaderlod_spatial_adapter_spread(ivec2 origin, int side);
ShaderlodSpatialPlan shaderlod_spatial_adapter_plan(float distance_blocks);
vec4 shaderlod_spatial_adapter_evaluate_linear(ivec2 pixel, ShaderlodSpatialSurface surface);
ShaderlodSpatialCache shaderlod_spatial_adapter_cache(int side, ivec2 tile_coordinate);
```

`surface` supplies current-frame camera-relative **view-space blocks**, a normalized
normal in that same space, a nonnegative adapter-defined factorization class,
normalized lightmap and explicit receiver protection. Protection includes sky,
hand, invalid depth, overlays, unsupported material/projection/DH paths and all
other exclusions required by the declared factorization. Every member and pair
passes the existing guard, including interior pixels at 4 × 4. The kernel rejects
incomplete edge tiles before any out-of-bounds surface callback. Spread probes
must describe all members/relevant reconstruction neighborhoods; availability=false
makes no lighting-edge assertion. The adapter must not reconstruct invalid depth
into a benign position and thereby accidentally mark it eligible.

`plan` calls the shared planner with the adapter's immutable current-frame policy,
capability/quality/protection inputs and declared rate mask. Distances are radial
Euclidean lengths in blocks, never raw depth or view Z. The producer passes the
minimum distance across all tile members. The consumer replans at the minimum
across its active reconstruction tiles; if this introduces an unprepared tier,
it selects full. Producer/consumer policy and surface snapshots must agree.
A separately supplied `near_blocks` guard protects every member through an
adapter-declared full-quality distance; invalid guards retain original shading.

`evaluate_linear` supplies **albedo-independent irradiance or another explicitly
declared linear vec4 basis**. All channels must permit the same linear sum and
units. The quantity key identifies that exact basis/units; it does not authorize
arbitrary shading factors. Nonlinear BRDF, normal, visibility decisions, tone
mapping or final RGB colors cannot be cached and reinterpreted by this kernel.
No dividing final shaded color by representative albedo. Full-resolution albedo,
material decoding, emission, specular/reflections, fog and final composition
remain at the recipient pixel. If a declared irradiance includes representative
AO/shadow, that spatial approximation must be disclosed and tested; full sample
counts at a representative do not preserve all recipient shadow detail.

Callbacks reached from representative or fallback-dependent control flow must
use derivative-free data or reviewed explicit gradients/LOD and sampler state.
The kernel cannot make implicit derivatives valid. Establish gradients before
divergent flow if the adapter needs them; no unreviewed `texture` sampling belongs
inside `evaluate_linear` or `surface` callbacks under these branches.

## Producer, storage and consumer obligations

The public producer entry is:

```glsl
ShaderlodSpatialCache shaderlod_spatial_produce(bool enabled, bool cache_contract_valid, int side,
    ivec2 tile_coordinate, ivec2 dimensions, float near_blocks,
    ShaderlodRegionLimits limits, int quantity_key, int epoch);
```

`dimensions` describes rendered surface pixels, not display resolution. Legal
sides are 2 and 4: half and quarter dimensions on each axis, nominally one
evaluation per 4 or 16 receiver pixels. Cache dimensions are `ceil(dimensions/side)`
per axis, computed by `shaderlod_spatial_cache_dimensions`. Tile origin is
`tile_coordinate*side`. The deterministic representative is
`origin + ((side-1)/2, (side-1)/2)`: offset (0,0) at side 2 and (1,1) at side 4.
There is no random phase or temporal rotation. Partial odd-edge tiles publish
invalid entries and reconstruct at full resolution.

The producer classifies first, queries the shared plan at minimum member distance,
and evaluates once only if that tier has positive weight. Disabled producer,
unsupported/invalid plan, rejected region or undemanded tier publishes invalid
without evaluating. `linear_quantity` is accepted only if finite.

A real adapter must provide distinct current-frame lower-rate producer draws,
legal output attachments and a later full-resolution consumer draw. Neighboring
fragments cannot share the representative result during the same draw on GL 4.1.
The kernel owns no pass numbering, attachment index, viewport allocation or format.
Audit exact pinned Iris/pack source graph, attachment lifetimes, render-target
lists, clear/ping-pong behavior, texture dimensions, limits, read/write hazards,
DH/projection variants and sampler coordinates before integration. Render a 2 × 2
producer over its half-size cache viewport and a 4 × 4 producer over its quarter-size
viewport, or use another explicitly proved allocation with matching pixel mapping.
Never shrink unrelated full-resolution gbuffer attachments. Every reachable entry
must be written/cleared invalid each frame, including rejected or disabled tiles.
The consumer reads only completed producer outputs, with nearest integer tile
addressing; never bilinear-filter validity or cross an invalid tile hole.

`ShaderlodSpatialCache` is a producer certificate containing validity, integer
quantity key, epoch, side and tile coordinates, plus the minimum member distance
in blocks. The library sets validity only after all members pass the guard and
the declared representative evaluation is finite. Store metadata in an exact
representable integer attachment (e.g. a reviewed integer texture using integer fetch), or an adapter-proved exact packing and
collision policy. Half-float tags cannot prove current epoch equality. An epoch
must change on frame, resize, source/options/policy reload and any camera/world
change invalidating inputs; producer and consumer share it. Define overflow/wrap
and prevent old entries surviving a reused epoch (clear/reset); signed integer
increment overflow is not an acceptable implicit policy. The library compares
exact supplied ints, but cannot verify attachment format, freshness or resource
ownership. Store minimum distance as exact binary32 (e.g. R32F) or prove a
conservative rounding policy that never increases it. An approximate distance
rounded upward can authorize a later tier incorrectly. RGB precision/format and
its quality error also remain adapter duties.

`cache_contract_valid` is an explicit adapter proof/gate for supported exact
metadata storage, current dimensions/attachments, completed ordered producer
writes and one **immutable surface, protection, policy and guard snapshot** shared
by both stages. False rejects before any callback. A bare valid bit does not prove
geometry unchanged: rewriting depth/material/protection between stages, failing
to bump/reset the epoch after changes or decoding approximate tags invalidates
this contract and must select full. Full-resolution material composition remains
per pixel outside this kernel; excluded/protected receivers were certified at
producer time, and the immutable snapshot is what makes that certificate usable.

The full-resolution consumer entry is:

```glsl
ShaderlodSpatialResult shaderlod_spatial_resolve(bool cache_contract_valid,
    ivec2 pixel, ivec2 dimensions,
    ShaderlodSpatialPlan initial_plan, float near_blocks,
    ShaderlodRegionLimits limits, int quantity_key, int epoch);
```

Supply an initial shared plan from the pixel's already validated radial distance.
The kernel checks complete tile bounds and validates exact rate, tile coordinates,
epoch, quantity, finite value and conservative minimum-distance certificates
**before** evaluating the full-resolution linear basis needed during a transition.
It replans at the minimum distance from demanded certificates. Each producer
classified every interior/edge member; the consumer performs no repeated region
reads or 120-pair classifier. A full-basis transition reads only the current pixel
and retains full fallback if that receiver is explicitly protected/invalid. Any
rejected region, invalid/stale/wrong-quantity cache or invalid plan returns
`full_resolution_required=true`: the adapter must execute its untouched original
full-resolution shading path. The result's zero placeholder is not black shading.
A unity/full/disabled plan exits without surface, cache or evaluation callbacks.
A disabled adapter should omit the producer passes as well; issuing empty draws
still incurs pass overhead and cannot establish disabled parity.

Accepted reconstruction is
`full_quantity*w.x + half_tile_quantity*w.y + quarter_tile_quantity*w.z`.
Weights come from the shared planner and are finite, nonnegative, normalized with
consistent active-tier flags. Reconstruction is piecewise constant within each
certified tile; the smooth blend is between tiers, not unguarded spatial bilinear
interpolation. If replanning needs an absent cache tier, full fallback is safe and
may increase work near transitions. Full↔half executes original basis plus half
producer work, and half↔quarter executes both producers; their sum can exceed a
single target rate. A producer 4 × 4 classification still performs up to
16 reads, 120 pair checks and 18 triangle checks once per tile. Those costs, exact
certificate storage, extra passes, cache reads, full fallback and both transition
paths must enter whole-frame GPU measurements.

# Distant diffuse lighting at a lower spatial rate

2026-10-05 source-only feasibility plan. No shader, builder, compiler, test,
archive or runtime changed. Photon remains the sole target. The density r2 pilot
reported original/off/on GPU means 15.4416/15.3720/14.9639 ms: one quality-changing
block is insufficient motivation for density calibration or evidence of the
1.5x-throughput goal. Investigate a larger opaque lighting region instead.

**Feasible first experiment:** evaluate complete original diffuse illumination
and receiver shadows once per valid distant 2×2 tile, cache an albedo-independent
coefficient, and multiply it by each pixel's original full-resolution material
albedo. Preserve full-resolution specular calculations, overlays, fog and cloud
composition. Near/unsafe pixels execute original shading. This requires a real
prepass/resolve graph and a spare texture with audited lifetime; it is not a
late branch around already computed lighting or a final-color blur.

The expensive region is not just `get_diffuse_lighting`. Before it, each terrain
pixel currently reads four AO and four AO-depth taps, reconstructs bent normal,
evaluates original filtered shadows and possibly SSRT, and constructs light
products. The reduced profile uses original PCF options 6–12 and SSRT option 10;
these are configured budgets, not measured executed fetch counts. Diffuse itself
adds directional/bounced light, SSS, sky/block light, darkness/night vision/cave
terms and material emission. Material decoding, sky/cloud/atmosphere processing,
specular, edge highlight and final composition would remain largely full rate.
No fresh reliable isolated cost/share is known for the removable region.

`get_diffuse_lighting` is not generally albedo independent: SSS uses albedo,
sheen includes its reciprocal, and emission may already encode albedo. Dividing
lit color by representative albedo is invalid and unstable at dark pixels.
First restrict to ordinary nonmetal, zero SSS/sheen/emission materials. For those
inputs, evaluate the original diffuse function with canonical white albedo and
zero exceptional fields; its result is the coefficient including `1/pi`.
Current full-resolution albedo then reproduces its high-frequency texture detail.
Do not extend this factorization to foliage, metals or emission by assumption.

## Two-pass implementation boundary

1. After original AO `deferred3`, run a quarter-pixel-count lighting prepass.
   Cache one coefficient per 2×2 tile. Cheap validity checks precede all AO
   reconstruction, PCF/SSRT and diffuse work. Invalid/near tiles write invalid
   alpha and perform no expensive lighting.
2. Full-resolution resolve decodes current material/albedo as upstream. A valid
   far tile supplies coefficient RGB and representative scalar shadow in A;
   otherwise execute the untouched full-rate lighting region. Highlights and
   reflections retain each pixel's current material, normal, view direction and
   original functions. Eligible rough surfaces reuse the scalar receiver-shadow
   factor; strong specular/reflection surfaces fall back to fully original shading.

The first cache allows only `SHADOW_COLOR=false`, so receiver shadow RGB is a
single scalar. Use alpha `<0` for invalid and `[0,1]` for that scalar. No colored
shadow approximation or missing-shadow fallback. Original AO reconstruction,
PCF/SSRT counts/distribution/radius and diffuse function execute at the computed
representative; shadow casters, sunlight cadence and shadow-map refresh are
unchanged. This still approximates spatial lighting between representatives.

Prototype material whitelist should initially be raw material mask 0 under the
verified reduced options. Its pinned branch has no SSS/emission/metal behavior;
cheap raw packed-field tests avoid running the full expensive material helper
four extra times in the classifier. Resolve still runs that helper per pixel.
Reject any options that invalidate this interpretation; widening the whitelist
requires explicit source proof and quality evidence.

## Classifier, transitions and temporal behavior

Use stable screen tile origin `2*(pixel/2)` and a fixed representative phase,
initially `(0,0)`. No frame-rotating sample phase/history cache. Evaluate every
frame using the current original projection/jitter; let upstream TAA accumulate
as usual. Fixed tiling still needs motion tests for swimming and shadow flicker.

All four tile members must be in bounds, terrain, non-hand, the approved material
class and lightmap range; reject overlays, moving entities/special masks, water,
wetness/puddles, material maps, strong specular/reflection surfaces and nonfinite
inputs. Compare reconstructed positions against the representative surface plane,
not merely raw depth or equal Z on sloped ground; check decoded normal agreement
and lightmap differences. Start with conservative tolerances and expose them as
private adapter parameters. Odd viewport edges and failed weights use original.

Geometry/material agreement cannot detect a cast-shadow edge on a flat surface.
Consider one original center shadow comparison per tile member plus local
AO/bent-normal variation as inexpensive practical lighting-edge rejection.
Measure this cost; it can reduce the gain. It is not a proof of PCF/SSRT spatial
equivalence. Reject uncertain penumbra/contact regions and inspect thin foliage
shadows, ground shadow boundaries and animated shadows early. Budget preservation
at representatives alone does not preserve visible spatial shadow detail.

Distance is radial camera/view-space blocks, conservatively the minimum of all
four member distances. Near tiles always use full rate. A centered distance band
can blend the coefficient/receiver-shadow factor with original full shading;
transition pixels pay both evaluations. Fully far, valid tiles take only cache
lighting. Make that extra band cost explicit. A 2×2 screen tile is the spatial
footprint; distance does not prove lighting is low frequency, so validity/quality
checks remain necessary. No new derivatives inside divergent shading branches.

This first consumer has discrete rates K=4 or K=1 per four-pixel tile. Do not
claim a generic integer count cap of K=2/3 is consumed, or multiply lighting by a
retained-work ratio. A future OPAQUE_LIGHTING adapter can expose validated spatial
rate/distance controls; mod config, declarations and actual consumption stay
separate. Static approximation does not need new temporal-history interfaces.

## Minimal kill test and feasibility gate

Before substantial pass-graph work, a narrowly pinned **quality-changing cost
control** can replace only the eligible far lighting region with cheap declared
irradiance/scalar-shadow values, while retaining current albedo/material and
full-resolution specular functions/composition. Its scalar-shadow diagnostic
changes lighting, including highlight illumination; it establishes neither
quality parity nor an isolated effect budget. Keep near/invalid pixels original.
If even this aggressive regional upper-bound control has little repeated
frame-only GPU/total-frame signal, stop before a prepass/resolve implementation.

If the signal merits it, the smallest honest optimization test is the actual
K1 cache plus K4 fallback above. Preserve original/default-off controls; measure
global off/on with fixed scene/focus/warmup, quiet teams and balanced order.
Require near texture/albedo parity, stable distant surfaces, thin/material/depth
edges, cast-shadow/SSS/glint cases and motion/TAA before accepting little
discernible loss. Measure whole-frame GPU/total time including prepass and all
fallback/edge overhead. A debug accepted-tile map helps interpret eligible area,
but no eligible fraction, GPU saving or 50% target progress is established here.

The main risk is coverage: forest foliage/SSS, wet reflective coasts and near
geometry may mostly fall back, while all pixels still pay classification and
full-rate material work. The sampler/pass/format implementation cost is real.
Proceed only if the bounded far lighting region has materially useful measured
cost; otherwise widen neither quality loss nor architecture to rescue a weak
signal. The transferable strategy is reusable illumination sampling plus
full-resolution material resolve in explicit deferred adapters, not a universal
shader rewrite.

# Benchmark world reuse and retention

Use an existing prepared client for repeated runs. When an exact reset is needed,
use one stable loader/version/scene slot instead of creating timestamped instances:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout \
  --source-profile run-workloads/photon-ssr-cost-controls-r1/coastalwater/high \
  --slot neoforge-1211-coast
```

This prepares `run-workloads/world-pool/neoforge-1211-coast/client`. Repeating the
command resets that same client to the canonical inputs. It copies existing warm
world data; it does not generate another world. Keep run plans, results and captures
that must survive a reset in a separate report directory. Checkout is deliberately
destructive inside its manifested slot, requires the same source, and refuses an
unmanaged directory, live Minecraft client, owned runtime lane or locked save.
It copies and verifies a staged replacement before swapping the usable client,
then removes only its own prior copy. Ordinary copy/install failures restore the
previous client and receipt. An interrupted `.client-reset-*` tree retains any
prior client and blocks another reset until the owner checks termination, lane/
save locks and the exact staged/prior inputs; uncertain leftovers are preserved.

scene slot through the existing settings Apply/recovery flow. The checkout/session
lock path is validated on Mac; this does not establish Windows runtime support.

Maintained profile/world preparation uses `run_storage.copytree`. On APFS it uses
`clonefile` so unchanged data shares disk blocks and each copy remains independently
writable. Unsupported filesystems use a real copy; hardlinks are never used for
worlds. Source profiles do not bring along camera sequences, screenshots, logs,
world-backup ZIPs, save backups or downloads. Pool checkout copies only runtime
inputs and excludes stale workload reports. Legacy fresh-output preparers still
require fresh destinations; their scientific inputs are not silently reused.

General copies admit their full logical size, with **32 GiB free** remaining on the
destination filesystem and **96 GiB maximum** logical data under `run-workloads`.
Serialized storage admissions include existing captures and backups. A staged
reset checks full additional physical copy bytes while applying the logical
workload limit to the final replacement footprint. The finite Bliss recipe below
explicitly propagates its 512 MiB/1 GiB operation reserve through the same copy

## Distance, footprint, original counts and time

[Adapter wrapper](../shaderpacks/photon-volumetric-lod/shaders/include/shaderlod/photon_volume_adapter.glsl:371)
uses radial cloud-shell **entry** distance E = length(direction*dists.x/CLOUDS_SCALE)
in blocks, not terrain distance. For 512/1536/128, the medium transition is
448–576 blocks and the far transition 1472–1600 blocks. Full medium ratio .85
applies between 576 and 1472; full far .75 starts at 1600. Below or at 448,
distance policy retains unity.

The finite final-pixel footprint lower bound is
`F = 2*E*(1/focal)*forward^2/(1 + forward/focal)`, where
`focal=max(abs(projection00)*view_res.x,abs(projection11)*view_res.y)` and
`forward=-(mat3(gbufferModelView)*direction).z > 0`. Feature scale is
`S = 1/(.005*max(noise_size)*CLOUDS_SCALE)` blocks. The footprint weight is
smoothstep(S,2S,F): F<=S yields original; F>=2S permits the full requested
reduction. This uses final view_res even with checkerboard cloud rendering.
No numeric E threshold follows without actual projection and noise allocation.

Overhead protection H=smoothstep(.35,.65,abs(direction.y)): full protection
at |direction.y|>=.65; partial restoration between .35 and .65. The viewer must
be below inner_radius-1 atmosphere unit, outside the cloud shell; inside/above
views fall back. Valid normalized directions, finite inputs, valid projection
and sampler size, positive shell interval <=2e4 atmosphere units and nonzero
coverage are required. The selected inner body still rejects planet/terrain
occlusion. These are eligibility heuristics, not visual parity proof.

Pinned original `shaders/include/sky/clouds/cumulus.glsl` uses
`N=uint(mix(primary_steps_horizon,primary_steps_zenith,abs(ray_dir.y)))`.
Canonical settings are horizon 40, zenith 20, direct-light 6 and ambient 2;
DEFERRED1 uses all of those (DEFERRED0 /2 is inactive in this consumer).
The nonnegative float-to-uint conversion truncates, so N=floor(40-20*|ray.y|)
subject to binary32 arithmetic. There is no random or time-dependent count
selection. Original samples entry+(i+jitter)*L/N and breaks when transmittance
falls below .075, or skips empty density; executed cells can therefore be <N.

[Shared target](../shaderpacks/common/shaders/include/shaderlod/volume_budget.glsl:12)
is clamp(mix(N,N*distance_ratio,footprint_weight*(1-H)),8,N). Its loop cap is
ceil(target), with a shortened final cell. Example N = 37/full medium weight:
.85 -> target 31.45/cap 32; full far .75 -> 27.75/cap 28. Binary32 thresholds,
quality restoration and floor 8 matter; reducing target may leave ceil unchanged.
Density strength is unchanged. Each cell uses its actual length for optical
depth; original scattering normalization is retained. Uniform-medium interval
integration does not prove heterogeneous-medium or early-exit parity.

Production primary jitter and checkerboard selection depend on frameCounter;
secondary jitter is hash2(fract(ray_pos)), hence changes with resampling.
Cloud wind/local coverage use world_age =
((worldDay %128)*24000+worldTime)/20, yielding 625 at day 0/time 12500. Day lock
does not freeze frameCounter, TAA terrain/depth, matrices or every sky input;
frameTimeCounter affects included sky/aurora. Existing diagnostic fixed primary
phase does not establish synchronized production rays.

# Git and artifact preservation

Track maintained source, tests, benchmark definitions, setup/configuration templates,
AGENTS.md, current state, indexed history, decisions and compact result summaries.
Keep credentials, machine-specific private settings, large models/data, raw captures,
logs and regenerable build caches outside Git. Ignored does not mean disposable.

## Current audit, 2026-11-05

Maintained source/document/configuration directories were checked for ignored files;
only expected generated/cache entries were found. Many useful files are untracked:
Git-visible is not committed, pushed or backed up. Review and commit them explicitly
before treating another clone as a complete copy. No commits or pushes were made.

- `experiment-evidence/fastpath/REPORT.md` and the small dependency preparation
  receipt are now Git-visible; raw report attachments are not thereby backed up.
- `dev/experiments/` includes frozen source copies, restoration inputs and raw
  evidence. It is not all disposable, despite being ignored.
- `run-workloads/` includes valuable canonical worlds as well as resettable clients.
  Preserve canonical worlds and recovery inputs separately before retiring copies.
- `dependencies/` contains pinned archives and local tools. Missing historical
  archives cannot necessarily be reconstructed from a filename or hash alone.

## At a milestone or machine handoff

Keep compact results and reusable code in ordinary Git-visible project directories.
For large valuable artifacts, record identity, location, purpose and recovery source
in the existing experiment/campaign record. Verify the recovery copy before deleting
the original. A second name, symlink, same-disk copy or an untested hash is not an
independent backup. No new per-run form or automatic cleanup is required.

This audit did not verify an independent backup of the ignored artifact trees.
Historical copies contain unique dirty/untracked work and must be reconciled before
retirement. Frozen source snapshots, nested repositories and third-party dependencies
retain their own history and exclusions; do not apply current rules over pinned runs.
Raw metadata inventories and audit limits are retained outside Git in the performing
agent's `~/.local/share/p-stack/repairs/20261105-ignore-audit/` receipt directory.

# Benchmark guide

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test \
  --profile /path/to/prepared/client \
  --pack /path/to/original-pack.zip \
  --pack-options /path/to/original-pack.zip.txt \
  --feature PUBLIC_OPTIMIZATION_ID \
  --output /path/to/fresh/report
```

On Linux ARM64 use `python3 scripts/linux_arm64_runtime.py benchmark test` with the same arguments. Select an existing loader/version/scene slot; keep the report outside that slot and on the same filesystem as the profile. Confirm the lane is free and the inputs match the intended tuple before launch. Do not reset a slot owned by a client or interrupted operation. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout --help` describes managed checkout. Use `run_storage.copytree` for profile/world copies; it enforces storage limits.

The standard test targets the prepared NeoForge 1.21.1 benchmark protocol. It renders native Off for 120 seconds before measurement, then acquires native Off, singleton candidate through normal Apply, then native Off return: 20 seconds each, with separate warmup, startup and recovery within a 900-second budget. Conditioning was added after repeated first-to-return drift; it does not prove stability. It records total-frame timing, drift, stills and restoration in the report. A valid slower result is still a result; a failed or invalid run is not a speed conclusion. Inspect `summary.json`, errors and restoration before proceeding. A short result is not proof of visual equivalence, DH/PBR compatibility or final closure. Compare matched total-frame measurements and disclose drift and scope.

G01 MakeUp copy elimination and G02 BSL mip elimination also collect existing untimed work witnesses after each measurement, disarming them before further timing. The BSL witness requires a separate untimed reload; inspect its completeness rather than inferring execution from parsed directives. G04 MakeUp `translucent_fastpath` requires `--saved-pose 9`: the maintained caller places one honey block in the backed-up save before all arms to cover the non-water/glass translucent class. Client visibility is checked; whole-save restoration removes the fixture after shutdown, including failed runs. Use `--width` and `--height` for the actual fullscreen mode (currently 2560×1600 on the local Asahi display).

BSL reflection and AO sample-reuse tests retain untimed draw-admission status; admission is not a saved-query count. Photon is validated by its separate pinned live-pixel-budget producer and manifest. Its generated solid-terrain program marker is checked at its exact declared value; unknown added options and changes to original native options still fail.

If the harness or inputs fail, preserve the failure, restore/release owned resources, fix the maintained harness or inputs, and retry. Do not copy harness code into report-local callers, inject launcher overrides, relax admission after failure, or substitute custom scripts for the standard result. Diagnostics are diagnostic and do not replace it. One Linux ARM64 BSL standard run completed with verified restoration and independent review; this does not establish behavior for other configurations or future changes. See [experiment history](EXPERIMENTS.md).

Keep reports, worlds, downloads, builds and captures out of Git. Do not kill unrelated processes. If restoration refuses due to unknown changes, preserve the data and inspect ownership and recovery before acting.

Runtime dependencies and original shader-pack inputs are stored under `dependencies/`. Keep active experiment output in `dev/experiments/` and any retained evidence in `experiment-evidence/`; both are local and outside Git. Prepared clients and worlds remain under `run-workloads/`.

# ShaderLOD project overview

ShaderLOD targets general-purpose, configurable distance quality control across
shader packs. Photon is the first implementation and performance proof. The first platform is NeoForge with Iris required. Photon is the
explicit compatibility target, and DH is optional for the mod while included
in the development runtime for compatibility checks.

The initial distance proposal is full quality through 32 blocks, medium quality
through 96 blocks, and low quality beyond that. These are starting defaults,
not a measured optimum. Define distance in camera-relative block units and
use transition bands or stable dithering to avoid a visible moving ring.

## Development sequence

1. Establish a reproducible NeoForge client skeleton and compatible Iris,
   Sodium, Photon, and DH runtime. Add durable goal/team infrastructure and a
   small LOD foundation that can be inspected and tested.
2. Prove one distance-sensitive Photon effect works under Iris with DH absent.
   Compare the same scene with the change disabled and enabled; inspect both
   visual transitions and GPU execution time before expanding infrastructure.
3. Build the Photon MVP around several measured effects. Candidate effects are
   POM/material work, shadow filtering, and SSR. Add validated configuration
   transport and useful quality presets as evidence supports them.
4. Extend LOD to DH terrain/water/shadows and validate the vanilla/DH boundary.
   Keep DH optional and test both installed and absent configurations.

## Architecture boundaries

The NeoForge client mod owns config, loader/runtime detection, and integration
lifecycle. Photon owns explicit GLSL LOD logic through a pinned, maintained
patch or derivative. Iris provides the shader runtime. DH extends terrain
rendering and eventually needs dedicated integration checks.

A Java config file does not automatically become an Iris custom uniform.

## CPU consumption, waits, GC and JIT

JDK thread load divides CPU time by wall duration and active processor count,
as shown in the [OpenJDK 21 implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openjdk/jdk21u/master/src/hotspot/share/jfr/periodic/jfrThreadCPULoadEvent.cpp).
The recording reports 14 hardware CPU threads. If that equals the active count,
render-thread load corresponds to approximately 92.5% of one CPU core, matching
6.411 ms × 144.12 FPS ≈ 92.4% from the separately exported clock records.
The Java and native render paths together consume substantial thread CPU.
This does not assign that CPU consumption to individual sampled methods.

The recording's aggregate JVM CPULoad is much lower than its render-thread load,
so those aggregate counters do not corroborate one another. The parser flags
the discrepancy; it must not be used to claim that the process was almost idle.
Machine-total CPU load averaged about 15.2% over capture. These trailing load
events do not measure GPU utilization or explain other runs' host state.

Three top-level GC pause intervals total 16.702 ms across the 40-second capture
(about 0.042% of wall duration); one pause is 12.318 ms. This can affect a few
frames but does not explain a sustained halving of throughput in this run.
There are no recorded render-thread park, monitor-enter, monitor-wait or sleep
events during capture. JDK profile settings threshold these at 10 ms, and native
driver waits are not Java monitor events, so shorter/native waits remain possible.

Four slow C2 compilations occurred during capture, including LevelRenderer and
the development overlay. Their durations are compiler-thread activity, not
render-thread pauses. Startup has much more compilation and GC, which is why
startup/warmup is not pooled with capture. Absence of other Compilation events
does not exclude JIT work below the profile's 100 ms threshold.

The useful next comparison is a similarly aligned recording from the **slow**
baseline, with unchanged scene/options and CPU-only clocks, plus host-state
telemetry owned by the coordinator. Compare culling/list contexts, native
submission/copy/swap contexts, CPU wall/thread ratios, waits, GC and compilation
by time bin. This recording alone cannot choose between driver behavior,
host scheduling/frequency, viewport invalidation or another cause of variability.

## Finding: expired deadline plus discovery failure spins and skips stop

**P2, source integration defect.** In the reviewed source,
`scripts/dev_client.py:394–424` performs process discovery, association and
readiness work before calling `deadline_stop`. Any exception in that work skips
the deadline handler. The catch retains ownership, which is appropriate, but
`scripts/dev_client.py:439–442` then computes a zero sleep interval once the
absolute deadline has passed and no request marker exists. Persistent probe
failure therefore causes repeated probes, manifest writes and logging with no
positive backoff, while neither a stop attempt nor a deadline refusal is
recorded. A verified live client can survive the deadline indefinitely.

Reproduction recipe for the parent-owned mocked supervisor test: supply a
future `stop_at_utc` at supervisor initialization, then advance mocked monotonic
time beyond its translated target. Let prelaunch process discovery succeed;
after launcher creation, make `process_table` raise `RuntimeError('probe
unavailable')` repeatedly. Bound execution by making mocked `time.sleep` raise
a sentinel `BaseException` after two calls. Observe sleep arguments `0`, absent
`deadline_stop_requested_utc`, and no invocation of the deadline handler.
This is a direct control-flow counterexample, not an executed runtime result.
The existing supervisor recovery test has no stop time and does not cover this
case; the deadline tests invoke the helper directly.

Recommended correction: arrange the due one-shot handler outside the discovery
try/except, retaining any existing proofs and relying on `stop` to independently
revalidate them. Missing proofs or failed validation must still refuse without
broadening targets or releasing ownership. Preserve positive backoff after a
due deadline on discovery failure. Parent was notified before runtime GO.

## Checked source boundary

- Omitted stop time remains persistent: plan stores `None`, the helper returns
  without signaling, and ordinary supervisor recovery retains the game/lock.
- `plan` validates malformed, naive, expired and more-than-12-hour times before
  session/config mutation. The supervisor validates again before preparation
  or launching; the stored field accepts an explicit timezone offset despite
  its `stop_at_utc` name. The supervisor translates once to a monotonic target,
  so later wall-clock changes do not move that target.
- Before the target, the helper does nothing. At the target, it publishes fresh
  proofs before invoking the existing exact-session stop. Its in-memory request
  marker prevents a second attempt, including after refusal.
- Stop validates all recorded live identities using PID, birth and argv plus
  profile association, then rechecks identity immediately before each SIGTERM.
  It targets game PIDs only; no group, launcher or shared daemon signal exists.
  PID/profile mismatch refuses. No forced-kill fallback exists.
- The loop uses its pre-stop process snapshot after a successful stop, so lock
  release can wait for another discovery iteration. That is conservative;

`observedName()` without translating its runtime/context failures into `Refusal`.

device/info. If those operations throw `RuntimeException`, public Apply catches
it before taking a config snapshot or creating a transaction, but follows generic
recovery and calls the real Iris reload with `selection == null`.

## Findings and reproduction

**P1, evidence false rejection:** `WorkloadInputs.jsonHash` hashes compact Gson
object serialization in insertion order. `ShaderLodEffectConfig` and
`SourceFingerprint` both use `Map.copyOf`, whose iteration order varies across
these actual JVMs. The actual OFF/ON effect objects and entire source qualification
objects are equal, but their serialized key orders differ and their exported
hashes differ. `ReceiptReplay.java` independently replays pinned Gson 2.10.1:
all four original hashes match their respective recorded object serialization;
recursive sorted-key hashes match between arms. Thus the original hashes are
valid raw serialization receipts, but unsuitable as semantic identity across
JVMs. Merely removing those fields loses a useful self-consistency check.

**P1, second ordering defect:** `PixelCoverageProbe.digestJson` also serializes
its complete receipt in object insertion order. Its `CANONICAL` Gson only
requests compact unescaped HTML output; it does not sort nested objects.
Canonicalizing the two nested digest fields alone cannot establish stable complete
receipt hashes. Sort object keys recursively for both derived and outer digests,
retaining array order, scalar types and values. Version the changed hash contract
and reject older incompatible receipts rather than force-convert r3 contracts.

**P2, known startup byte changes:** actual receipt diffs contain precisely 17
paths. Nine are timestamp/raw-SHA paths from the two known Iris properties
files (including duplicated configuration semantics and the top-level Iris SHA).
Six are raw length/SHA/text paths for `config/shaderlod-client-1.toml.bak` and its
duplicated semantic record. Two are the derived hashes above. The complete exact path list

Both captured properties files parse to identical complete Java Properties maps

original boundary report. Validate them before deriving a separate semantic
receipt. Keep inventory strict: adding/deleting an unknown file remains failure.

For the exact main TOML, authorize only the single boolean in the exact `[lod]`

## Runtime extraction contract

The sole client/GPU operator owns a fresh **untimed** diagnostic JVM with
`-Dshaderlod.dev.cloudSamplerProbe=true`, exact artifact/source pins, effective
options/config and a fresh profile log root. Preserve the raw report and client
logs. This observer can stall and must stay outside performance windows.

Extract each capability observation with its program ID, `timestamp_utc`,
`draw_origin`, linked status and scan bounds. The entry timestamp is captured
immediately before the program introspection; it is not an exact per-getter clock.
Origins are `iris-fullscreen-quad` or `sodium-raster-submission`; neither identifies
a shader stage or proves effect execution. A program is captured only at its first
observed draw, at most 64 numeric IDs per JVM. Uniform scans are bounded to 4096
entries and 1024-byte names. ID reuse/relinking does not produce another sample.

For example, this read-only extraction preserves raw field records without
converting missing state into a boolean or substituting configured values:

```sh

assert report.get("capability_uniform_schema") == 1, "fresh schema-1 report required"

    print(json.dumps({key: entry.get(key) for key in (
        "timestamp_utc", "current_program", "draw_origin", "linked",
        "active_uniform_count", "uniform_scan_truncated", "uniform_name_length_truncated",
        "capability_uniforms", "capture_failure", "active_texture_before", "active_texture_after"

PY
```

Accept typed observation only with actual inventory type `GL_INT` (5124), size 1,
nonnegative location and queried status. Evaluate actual protocol version 1 and

may initially expose unavailable state, and this first-draw observer cannot prove
settled or live-reload state. Do not replace an early 0 with a later supplier
readback or a source-based inference. Retain it with its actual time and origin.

The operator must inspect client logs for shader/link/GL/capture failures and
verify matching active texture before/after for completed sampler captures.
Relate a program to a particular consuming shader using separately pinned
source/hook evidence. Linked capability values alone do not prove the common
work decision ran, fewer physical integrations executed, or rendered quality and
total throughput passed. Driver compilation, actual consumer linkage, settled

# ShaderLOD development throughput review

October 12, 2026, Pacific time. Human-authorized investigation and improvements,
with a 60-minute elapsed budget and four GPT-6 Astra workers. The existing shader
runtime goal remains paused; this maintenance does not spend or reset its remaining
1,200-second allocation. Findings describe the sampled record, not an estimate of
total agent hours.

## Conclusion

The largest demonstrated opportunities are better delivery sequencing and reuse of
actual launcher/consumer contracts. The project already shares its shader policy,
selection/recovery service and adapter resources across ten builds. Another general
shader framework would not address the recurring problems we found.

Agents produced substantial real work, including old MakeUp/Sildur renderer gains
and newer rendering/control ports. But expensive validation and preparation often
advanced before a usable candidate, while some optimization ports targeted inactive
or very small workloads. Repeated hand-built caller assumptions then caused failures
that were unrelated to shader performance. The correction is to port a named working
mechanism through its actual selected consumer, automate repetitive authoring and
launch steps, and make the evidence required depend on the requested deliverable.

## What supports that conclusion

| Finding | Evidence and limitation | Practical consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Delivery ordering materially mattered | After explicit all-family manual-preview steering, ten JARs were ready in 49m38s. The preceding BSL source investigation occupied a 71-minute observed interval without optimizer acceptance. Different scopes mean this is not a controlled productivity ratio. | Deliver the requested preview with honest limitations; do not make an unrelated certification project its prerequisite. |
| Consumer assumptions repeatedly failed | Eight distinct caller/observer mismatches sampled: receipt path, loaded options, float serialization, stale assertion, readiness timing and other concrete joins. Several valid captures were salvaged without rerunning the client. | Replay actual saved producer/receipt shapes through changed code before its dependent launch. More synthetic tests of the wrong assumption do not help. |
| Deadline orchestration was a mechanical recurrence | One independently checked handoff left only 31 seconds at preflight, below the existing 130-second minimum. Earlier instances were already in USER_LESSONS. Later private operations fixed sequencing. | Maintain that final operation once; stamp only after preparation/review, then produce/freeze/preflight/launch without a model handoff. |
| Source coverage is not necessarily active optimization | BSL Aurora is off in the native reference. Astra AO12 remains12 under Balanced and becomes10 under Performance, but its original Mac rendering is blocked. Eligible Performance can select renderer batching instead of the generated shader graph. | State preset, selected route and active native work in each port assignment. Inactive-effect work is coverage, not evidence of speed. |

Six current Fabric26.1.2 brackets show no demonstrated gain, with native-return drift of 20–32%. | Reuse implementations and evidence for unchanged dependencies; measure benefit on the actual new tuple before quoting a percentage. |

# Spatial shading LOD: minimal mod interface

2026-10-05. Source-only proposal for the
[general 50% goal](goals/general-lod-50-percent.md), coordinated with
`lod_opportunities`' lower-rate `DISTANT_DIFFUSE_IRRADIANCE` investigation. Only
this document is owned by `effect_api`; no Java/config/GLSL/resource edits,
tests, compiler, archive or client ran. This proposal is not an accepted shader
consumer or performance/quality result.

**Recommend:** reuse the existing immutable distance/work policy and config shape,
with one additive `OPAQUE_LIGHTING` effect only when root selects an explicit
spatial consumer. Its first declared Photon capability is opaque diffuse
irradiance reconstruction. Keep albedo, material decoding, specular/reflections,
geometry and existing shadow/AO policy controls separate. A four-to-one evaluation
rate is a plausible quality/performance tradeoff worth testing; it does not need
a formal worst-case image-error proof before a bounded experiment.

## What the budget means

The adapter's upstream unit is four diffuse irradiance evaluations for one 2×2
tile of **rendered opaque pixels**, not four display pixels regardless of TAAU.
`mediumWorkRatio`/`farWorkRatio` request a retained evaluation fraction. The pure
policy can calculate `ceil(4 * retainedRatio)`, clamped to a legal floor of one;
1/.75/.5/.25 correspond to requested counts 4/3/2/1. Do not multiply irradiance,
AO strength, shadow visibility, radiance, light intensity or albedo by this ratio.
Geometry/material edge rejection raises the legal floor to four independently
of the requested distance budget.

Use the nearest camera-relative block distance among all four valid receivers.
Full near quality means a tile cannot lower its rate when any member needs full
near shading. A conservative first experiment may retain all four through the
entire centered near transition band. Keep the documented distinction between
full-near safety and the policy's continuous distance interpolation. The policy
does not decide receiver similarity, reconstruction weights or rate legality.

The selected initial experiment supports only counts one and four. Declare that
limitation: requests for two/three select original four-evaluation fallback until
matching representative patterns/storage are implemented. Do not claim their
caps or smooth spatial transitions were consumed. The first cost control can
apply one representative only beyond the completed far band; motion/transition
inspection must then decide whether to implement intermediate rates or a stable
tile-coherent transition schedule. Such a schedule requires a declared rate
mapping; it is not automatically provided by smooth ratios or TAA.

## Proposed mod surface

`MATERIALS` is the wrong existing category: its reference adapter controls
POM/material work, while this experiment retains full-rate material and albedo
reads. `SHADOW_FILTERING`/`AMBIENT_OCCLUSION` describe protected lighting
sampling; reusing those controls would imply that their current protection or
quality budgets authorize a spatial diffuse change. `VOLUMETRICS` is unrelated.
Reuse their implementation shape, not their semantic identities.

A future root-owned integration would add `OPAQUE_LIGHTING` with stable suffix
`OpaqueLighting` and config section `effects.opaque_lighting`. Reuse `mode`,
`near`, `far`, `transition`, `mediumWorkRatio` and `farWorkRatio`; no tile-size,
reconstruction-tolerance, registry or driver-specific public config is needed
for the first pinned 2×2 adapter. Adapter-owned fixed guards must be recorded
alongside source hashes. Keep defaults INHERIT, 32/96/8, unity ratios and the
existing protection setting. Experimental ADAPTIVE/far=.25 is opt-in, not a
promoted default.

Use extension **version 2** to make the new field group distinguishable from
version 1's six-effect/37-field source contract. Existing core version 2 and all
existing per-effect field names/mode numbers retain their meanings. The additive
effect adds six fields, giving 43 extension fields including the version:

| Proposed field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `shaderlodOpaqueLightingMode` | 0 INHERIT, 1 FULL, 2 ADAPTIVE |
| `shaderlodOpaqueLightingNear` | Full-to-medium centered boundary in blocks |
| `shaderlodOpaqueLightingFar` | Medium-to-far centered boundary in blocks |
| `shaderlodOpaqueLightingTransition` | Full centered band width |
| `shaderlodOpaqueLightingMediumWorkRatio` | Requested medium retained evaluation fraction |
| `shaderlodOpaqueLightingFarWorkRatio` | Requested far retained evaluation fraction |

The new consumer must require its exact accepted extension version, valid fields
and core global enable before reducing work. Absent mod/version 1/unknown mode,
unsupported pinned source, FULL or invalid conversion selects original full-rate
shading. INHERIT preserves the adapter's original/default pack policy, which is
full rate in this proposed adapter. An old version-1 consumer must explicitly
review version-2 acceptance; changing the number alone cannot establish support.
No new capability uniform or automatic shader rewriting is proposed.

Do not add OPAQUE_LIGHTING to the shadow/AO budget-cut category merely because
it participates in opaque lighting. Its separate opt-in controls spatial
diffuse evaluation; existing shadow/AO protections remain true and keep their
sample budgets/radii/strengths unchanged. The adapter must independently describe
whether its reconstructed quantity includes shadow/AO modulation. Keeping their
budgets full does not by itself prove unchanged spatial shadow detail.

## Photon material and reconstruction boundary

Pinned `d4_deferred_shading.fsh:335–367` decodes per-pixel albedo, material mask,
flat normal and lightmap levels. `material.glsl` additionally carries emission,
roughness, SSS/sheen, porosity, metal flags and specular parameters; a matching
material mask alone is not a similarity certificate. Current reduced Mac options
disable normal/specular mapping, but that cannot be assumed for future profiles.

`get_diffuse_lighting` is not already a clean albedo-independent irradiance
function: SSS/sheen uses albedo, emission is added before its final albedo factor,
and the metal diffuse correction is material-dependent. Do not cache its final
RGB and divide by representative albedo. Factor only an explicitly reviewed
irradiance component, or initially restrict eligible receivers to simple opaque
nonmetal, nonemissive, non-SSS, unmapped materials. Retain the original material
emission, SSS, specular/reflection and local lighting composition where applicable.
Multiply reconstructed irradiance by each recipient's own full-resolution albedo.
Albedo texture variation itself need not reject an otherwise coherent tile: that
detail is intentionally retained at full rate.

The four-member classifier must reject sky/hand, water/translucency, overlay/
entity mismatch, invalid/out-of-bounds receivers, depth discontinuities, facing/
normal discontinuities, materially different lighting parameters and incompatible
lightmap levels. Begin with DH disabled; DH/vanilla projection boundaries select
full original until explicitly implemented. Use linear/view-space depth or a
receiver-plane test, not a raw reversed-depth delta. Guard normal/material/
lightmap variation independently; distance alone cannot authorize cross-surface
reuse. Guard thresholds are pragmatic starting values requiring quality tuning,
not an exactness requirement that forbids the experiment.

The shader owner selected **combined diffuse irradiance with representative
upstream shadow/AO**, rather than sharing only cheap sky/blocklight arithmetic.
Initially exclude SSS/sheen/emission/metals, mapped/wet materials, strong specular/
reflection paths, overlays/hand/sky and DH boundaries. Store irradiance RGB and
scalar opaque shadow in alpha; colored shadows stay outside the initial consumer.
Per-recipient albedo and eligible specular math remain full resolution, but using
the representative shadow factor in that math is still a spatial approximation.
All original shadow/AO counts, radii and strength parameters remain unchanged for
each evaluated representative; this does not mean all four original spatial
lighting evaluations occurred.

AO/bent-normal and shadow inputs can vary on a tile containing one smooth
geometric surface. Full-resolution albedo and a geometry-only classifier cannot
preserve a cast-shadow boundary by themselves. Declare this limitation and inspect
cast-shadow/foliage motion early. If it produces visible failures, a pragmatic
next guard can compare existing reconstructed AO variation and cheap center-shadow
comparisons across the four members, rejecting large spreads or ambiguous edge
values. This is a practical quality guard to tune, not a formal no-occluder proof;

Atmosphere positions, shell intersections and step lengths retain Photon's native

obtain camera-relative blocks. It uses final-resolution `view_res`, projection
focal scales and view-ray foreshortening to derive a conservative finite-pixel
cone bound, without fragment derivatives. The fine-noise texture's actual base
level dimensions supply a voxel feature scale:
`1 / (0.005 * max(textureSize) * CLOUDS_SCALE)` blocks. That is a conservative
eligibility heuristic; nonlinear shaping means it does not prove that density is
band limited or that sample reduction is imperceptible. Reduction smoothly starts
when the smallest pixel footprint exceeds one voxel and reaches its policy cap
at two voxels. Narrower footprints retain original work.

Inside/above the physical cloud shell, including one atmosphere unit of boundary
rounding protection, retains full work. World-space overhead views restore full
work smoothly over `abs(ray.y)=0.35..0.65`; >=0.65 remains original. Actual volume
entry controls the distance bands, so cloud geometry beginning near the viewer
retains its near integration rather than being classified by the far endpoint.
This does not discard a near interval to manufacture savings.

Distance, footprint and overhead weights combine into a **continuous** retained
work target; no frame-noise count selector is added. A count target q allocates
ceil(q) cells of width interval/q, shortening the final cell to the remaining
interval. Each sample uses the original primary jitter within its own cell. Every
optical-depth term multiplies the actual cell length, and apparent-distance
weights also include cell length so the short last cell is not overrepresented.
Configured cell lengths sum to the unchanged full ray interval, subject to the
same upstream transmittance early exit. No density, extinction, scattering
coefficient or fog strength is reduced. Integer q recovers ordinary equal-width
quadrature; at integer count crossings the last cell's contribution tends to0.
Upstream phase functions, secondary illumination and distance fade laws remain.

# Receiver continuity for distant shading regions

2026-10-05. Original ShaderLOD MIT helper:
`shaderpacks/common/shaders/include/shaderlod/surface_region_continuity.glsl`,
SHA-256 `497c38b723df0255e9b07b5b62e695d644f0d0eb19538f14db5f95846e9cc040`.
It implements a reusable geometry/material eligibility gate for explicit
distance-dependent shading-frequency adapters. Existing 2×2 helper, Photon
sources, Java transport and runtime are unchanged by this contribution. This
helper has no uniforms, samplers, derivatives, transport or shader-pack names.

## Exact integration contract

```glsl
bool shaderlod_surface_region_eligible(
    bool enabled, int region_width,
    vec3 positions_view[16], vec3 normals_view[16], int material_ids[16],
    vec2 lightmaps[16], bool protected_members[16], float near_blocks,
    bool lighting_spread_available, vec2 ao_shadow_spread,
    ShaderlodRegionLimits limits);
```

`shaderlod_region_default_limits()` constructs the conservative defaults below.
The helper is standalone; an adapter copies this exact owned source into its
explicit include tree, records its hash/license and includes it once. Repeated
inclusion is guarded with `#if !defined` to avoid Iris boolean-option discovery
leaks. It does not modify or rewrite arbitrary shaders.

Array storage is fixed at16 elements for GLSL4.1. The active members are the first
`region_width*region_width` elements, **packed row-major with stride=region_width**.
Width2 therefore uses indices0…3, not a subset at stride4. Initialize inactive
padding to benign values even though the function does not inspect it. Width4
uses all16. Width1 explicitly returns false for original full-rate shading;
unsupported widths, disabled controls and invalid limits also return false.
**False always requires the untouched original full-resolution lighting path.**

All positions are camera-relative **view-space blocks** and normals are normalized
in the **same view space**. Normals should represent receiver geometry; a world
normal must be rotated into view space by the adapter before use. Positions
reconstruct receiver geometry from already validated current-frame depth. The
helper compares position separations along receiver normals, which permits
planar slopes with unequal view Z; it does not require equal raw/linear depth.
Raw invalid/sky depth is not recognizable from a finite placeholder position:
the adapter must flag it or reject the region before this call.

Material IDs are nonnegative adapter-defined factorization classes, and all must
match. Matching IDs alone do not establish diffuse factorability. Each actual
consumer must still exclude SSS/sheen/emission/metals, strong specular/reflections,
wetness and incompatible material maps. Normal/lightmap/geometry agreement is
separate from that material proof.

`protected_members` covers each sky, hand, invalid-depth, out-of-bounds odd-region
edge, overlay, special or otherwise unsupported receiver. Any protected member
rejects the whole region. Every member must be radially farther than `near_blocks`;
the minimum distance governs near protection. No foreground/sky/hand member is
blurred into the region by this helper, and no subset of accepted corners can
license a failed interior pixel.

## All-member geometric checks and limits

Every active member is checked for finite positions/normals/lightmaps, position
components within±65536 blocks, normal squared-length error≤0.001, normalized
lightmap channels[0,1], matching material and near/protected status. Every pair
is checked for distinct position, normal agreement, lightmap agreement and
normal-projected plane separation in **both** member normals. Width4 has120 pair
checks; these are real classifier work, not an assumed free proof.

Every local screen cell is checked, including all nine interior/outer cells at
width4. Each cell's two triangles must have nonzero/non-singular area, distinct
adjacent edges and consistent winding. Coincident, collinear or folded geometry
returns original. The smallest adjacent pixel-edge length across **all** cells
sets the footprint-scaled tolerance, so increasing a region to4×4 does not loosen
plane eligibility merely by increasing its overall span.

| Limit | Default | Units / meaning |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `plane_absolute_blocks` | 0.015 | Absolute normal separation in blocks |
| `plane_relative` | 0.015 | Additional separation per block of the smallest adjacent pixel edge |
| `plane_max_blocks` | 0.08 | Hard cap on total separation, independent of world distance/region width |
| `minimum_normal_cosine` | 0.995 | Minimum pairwise supplied normal dot product, nominally about5.7° |
| `maximum_lightmap_delta` | 1/255 | Maximum pairwise normalized difference per channel |
| `minimum_area_ratio` | 0.0001 | Triangle area divided by its adjacent edge lengths, dimensionless |
| `maximum_ao_shadow_spread` | (0.10,0.025) | Optional normalized max-minus-min AO/shadow threshold |

Minimum edge/pair length is0.000001 blocks. All limits are range/finite checked;
invalid policy data never silently broadens eligibility. Defaults are conservative
starting points for quality testing, not demonstrated safe universal thresholds
or a formal error certificate. Binary32 precision loss that collapses coordinates
to singular geometry retains original shading.

Optional AO/shadow spread must already describe the **complete receiver region**
or be supplied by an explicitly measured adapter probe. With availability=false,
the helper makes no lighting-edge check. Even finite low spread is heuristic:
geometry agreement cannot detect a thin cast shadow on a planar surface, and
finite receiver probes may all miss it. Derive the union of all original receiver
reconstruction neighborhoods using the adapter's actual sampling coordinates.
Do not check only representative taps or assumed corner samples. The consuming
adapter owns actual texture dimensions, bounds and AO/shadow input collection.

## Work avoidance, transitions and quality

Run this gate before representative expensive lighting. The adapter supplies its
own stable screen-region origin, radial LOD bands, discrete evaluation-rate
selection and original fallback. This helper performs no texture fetch, lighting,
albedo sampling, sample-phase rotation, history reuse, rate selection or blur.

For factorable diffuse lighting, share an albedo-independent coefficient while
retaining each pixel's original full-resolution material/albedo, specular,
reflections, overlays and final composition. A4×4 representative is an explicit
spatial approximation. Shared shadow/highlight visibility or half-float cache
precision must be disclosed by the adapter and inspected independently.

The helper supplies no distance blend. The adapter owns centered transition
bands, minimum-region distance and stable phase. Transition pixels blending
cached and original lighting must evaluate both; failed regions remain wholly
original. Never interpolate through invalid cache holes or apply bilinear reuse
across foreground/material/sky boundaries. Geometry/material agreement does not
prove lighting frequency is low enough, even far from the camera.

## Captured state and limits

Output is `<gameDirectory>/logs/cloud-sampler-state.json`, inside ignored
runtime directories. It is rewritten through a temporary file after each new
program. It includes UTC timestamps, GL version/renderer/vendor/GLSL version,
context support flags, and at most 64 unique nonzero numeric program IDs per
JVM. Numeric ID reuse after shader reload will not create a new record; use a
fresh JVM for each shader configuration. There is a 4096-active-uniform scan
limit per program, with truncation explicit in the report.

The `samplers` object retains the watched aliases, including their explicit
missing/inactive entries, and also captures every active scalar `sampler2D`
and `sampler3D` found within the bounded linked-uniform scan. Linked names and
existing JSON field names are preserved; `linked_uniforms` retains the scanned
type/size inventory. Other sampler types (including `sampler2DShadow`) and
sampler arrays outside the watched aliases are inventory only; watched
unsupported types/arrays receive an explicit unknown binding.

Each selected active scalar sampler has its linked type/name/size/location,
`glGetUniformi` unit, bound texture ID and 2D/3D target. The texture object's
min/mag filters, base/max levels, min/max LOD, LOD bias and supported anisotropy
are recorded. If sampler objects are supported, the unit's indexed
`GL_SAMPLER_BINDING` is queried. A nonzero sampler object contributes its own
filter/LOD/bias/anisotropy parameters as the effective sampling parameters;
texture base/max levels still belong to the texture. Allocated mip images and
texture completeness are not queried. Unknown/missing/inactive/unsupported
fields are explicit and cannot be interpreted as safe sampling.

The probe only changes `GL_ACTIVE_TEXTURE` temporarily and restores the actual
prior value in `finally`. It uses raw GL activation and restoration, so it does
not alter Minecraft's cached active-unit bookkeeping. It never binds a texture,
sampler, framebuffer or program, changes texture/sampler parameters, calls
`glFinish`, creates GPU queries, or consumes `glGetError`. Legal queries are
capability/type guarded; Java query failures are recorded or stop the probe.
Driver GL errors are not detected by return values alone, so the report labels
queried values as unchecked and the owner must inspect GL/runtime logs.

The first draw's bindings can differ from later weather/options/pipeline state.
A finite snapshot cannot prove branch uniformity, defined implicit gradients,
all cloud layers/options, or harmless literal-count dispatch. Missing cloud
samplers in one profile mean missing evidence for that density path. A sampling
review must combine this snapshot with exact source/GLSL rules and retain any
unresolved derivative behavior as a blocker for the literal probe.

# Four-phase live-bridge control in one JVM

Source-only proposal, 2026-10-04. No code, build, profile, shader reload or capture
was performed for this design. The coordinator's running matrix remains the
only GPU owner. This control addresses between-launch variability and possible
live-bridge scaffolding costs; it does not establish a performance improvement.

## Question and fixed rendering workload

Run one already-prepared all-five-effects-off Photon candidate and change only
`ShaderLodConfig.ENABLED` between four phases: OFF/ON/OFF/ON. Keep one JVM, world,
camera, shader-pack archive, effective shader options, shader pipeline and
compiled programs. Do not reload shaders, switch packs or recopy a save between
phases. All other production config values remain fixed.

Use a pinned **no-atmosphere-guard** archive. Current shared source contains
`shaderlod_needs_atmosphere`: without border fog/blocky clouds its terrain result
is `depth == 1.0 || !shaderlod_enabled()`. A structural candidate can therefore
change atmosphere work when global enablement changes even with all five effect
switches false. That would invalidate this workload. Verify the selected archive
actually retains the original unconditional `d4_deferred_shading` atmosphere
call; a helper declaration alone is not evidence of an active call. Record the
exact archive hash and build metadata, not merely a filename containing
"no-atmosphere".

Required effective pack controls are:

| Control | Required value |
| --- | --- |
| `SHADERLOD_CLOUDS`, `SHADERLOD_WATER`, `SHADERLOD_FOG`, `SHADERLOD_SSR`, `SHADERLOD_MATERIALS` | false |
| `SHADERLOD_USE_MOD_CONFIG` | true |
| `SHADERLOD_PRESERVE_LIGHTING` | true |
| `SHADERLOD_CACHED_SKY`, `SHADERLOD_WATER_ANALYTIC`, `SHADERLOD_DEBUG` | false |
| Mod debug | false throughout |
| Terrain policy and warmed-scene confirmation | false |
| `rendering.optimizeShadowCulling`, `rendering.separateShadowVisibilityLists` | false |

The main mod is present in every phase. Off/on is a runtime uniform/config
control, distinct from removing the mod or recompiling a pack with different
macros. Keep all upstream quality options identical, including reflections,
cloud resolution, ray counts and any material resource packs. Use an inspected
fixed-camera scene; shoreline clear weather with fixed shader wetness 0 is one
practical initial control. Storm needs a separate matched fixed-wetness 1 run.
Actual Minecraft rain and day/world-age values remain unchanged within a
session. FrameCounter, frameTime and animation clocks continue normally.

## Remaining scaffolding that must be acknowledged

The five switches own cloud, water, fog, SSR and materials. They do not globally
remove every ShaderLOD expression. Current explicit source still:

- Computes a generic `shaderlod_quality_at` in deferred lighting and passes one
  from translucent shading. With `SHADERLOD_PRESERVE_LIGHTING`, PCF/SSRT/GTAO/SSAO
  select tier zero and original budgets; source-level tier expressions can
  remain before optimization. Do not assume the driver eliminates all of them.
- Retains the deferred debug branch
  `if (shaderlod_debug_enabled() && !is_hand)`. The debug helper reads its bridge
  flag independently of global enablement. Debug false must be verified from
  config/observations; global OFF is not a substitute for disabling debug.
- Retains uniform declarations and the bridge sentinel. `shaderlod_quality_at`
  returns early when disabled, while enabled can compute generic tiers even
  when no effect changes its final work. This is the specific scaffolding/code
  path difference the proposed control can expose.

`CommonUniformsMixin` registers bridge version 2, enabled, preset, near/far,
transition and debug at `PER_FRAME`. Several getters construct a validated
`ShaderLodConfig.snapshot()`. Only the enabled value changes here; the other
getters and registrations remain present. Supplier execution or intended config
values do not, by themselves, prove a GPU uniform upload or active linked
uniform. Some unused uniforms can be optimized out. If a bounded observer is
added, observe the existing registered integer supplier before returning its
original value; do not reevaluate it at report time or infer linked uniform
state from one registration log. Identify observed versus unobserved suppliers.

The global flag also changes CPU short-circuit paths:
`GeometryLodController` evaluates enabled before terrain-enabled, and
`ShadowCullingRuntime` evaluates enabled before its optimization flag. Keeping
these features false prevents geometry/culling/list-ownership work changes, but an extra config
read on ON is still possible. Commands/runtime-status reporting may log one
flag transition; the settling interval excludes that transition from capture.
Therefore any ON/OFF difference measures the complete live-flag/scaffolding
path, not exclusively the cost of one GLSL branch or `glUniform` call.

"Same workload" here means preserved effect budgets and expected rendering
behavior under these controls. It does not claim byte-identical source to
original Photon, pixel-identical temporal frames, or equal instruction counts.

## Bounded upgrade to the existing session

Upgrade `BenchmarkSession` rather than creating a second world/client/bootstrap
framework. Today it alternates four phases, uses fixed 8-second switch settling
and 20-second capture, stores raw CPU/GPU lists, and restores enabled=true at the
end. It lacks per-phase elapsed/frame counts, current input fingerprints,
window/wetness exports and fresh phase identities. `ComparisonClient` already
ignores control-file `enabled` while a benchmark owns the flag, but other camera,
preset/debug/terrain fields can still change; reject those changes while
capturing. Reject simultaneous benchmark and workload capture at entry.

Suggested initial parameters: 45–60 seconds initial warmup, four phases,
8 seconds settling and 20 seconds capture per phase. This is roughly three
minutes after one JVM startup, with no reload/bootstrap between phases.
Accept an explicit starting order; the first run is OFF/ON/OFF/ON. A later
ON/OFF/ON/OFF session checks ordering drift, not independent frame replicates.
Save the initial enabled value and restore it on completion/failure instead of
unconditionally setting true. Do not persist temporary phase values or alter
other user config. Restore only after the last image/query collection has ended.

A small state machine is enough:

1. Validate eligibility, record session UUID/fingerprints, initialize fixed
   weather policy from startup and warm the one scene.
2. Set expected enabled state on the client/render thread; record a unique phase
   UUID and switch frame/time. Start settling; keep rendering and clocks normal.
3. At capture start, reset `GpuTimers`/`CpuTimers` samples and record their new
   epochs. `GpuTimers.resetSamples()` currently advances its epoch and resets CPU
   history; old pending results are discarded by epoch filtering. Record actual
   frame ID after reset; do not reset Iris frameCounter or histories.
4. Begin a fresh `ShaderInputTracker` measurement window and a per-phase window
   tracker. Record input/temporal snapshots. `beginMeasurement()` clears observed
   ranges/read counts without calling any original wetness supplier. Keep the

## Readback and restoration procedure

Opt in with `shaderlod.dev.pixelCoverage=true`. Explicitly set `gpuTiming`, `cpuTiming`
and `cpuLayerTiming` false; benchmark modes are forbidden. The utility's property
gate performs no GL or file I/O. Root must apply it before installing/arming
the capture and preserve it for the full run.

Save actual state before mutation: current program, draw/read FBO bindings,
four viewport values, active texture unit, that unit's `GL_TEXTURE_BINDING_2D`,
`GL_PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER_BINDING`, and all eight pack fields: ALIGNMENT, ROW_LENGTH,
SKIP_ROWS, SKIP_PIXELS, SWAP_BYTES, LSB_FIRST, IMAGE_HEIGHT and SKIP_IMAGES.
Do not change active unit. Bind the known existing texture on the already-active
unit, query level 0 with `glGetTexLevelParameteri`, set pack PBO 0 and tight pack
(alignment 1, other seven fields 0). Use a direct native float buffer of exactly
`width * height` floats. `fillSentinel` fills all lanes with NaN without moving
the buffer's position. Call
`GL11.glGetTexImage(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0, GL_DEPTH_COMPONENT, GL_FLOAT, buffer)` once.
Capture whether that call actually returned. Copy all lanes in OpenGL row order;
do not flip, downsample, tone-map, sparsely sample or infer unread pixels.

In `finally`, independently attempt restoring every saved pack field, pack PBO,
and prior active-unit 2D binding. If a restore operation throws, retain its error
and continue other restores. Verify active unit and all saved state again,
including the otherwise untouched FBO/program/viewport. Capture before/after
`State` plus each error in `Restoration`. The utility rejects changed state,
missing pack fields, unreturned readback, wrong depth storage/level/object,
non-native extents, and any nonfinite or out-of-range depth lane. NaN sentinel
guards a no-op/truncated native read; GL error flags are not consumed by this
utility. Root's wrapper must preserve read/restore exceptions and raw failure
metadata, never turn an exception into a cleared plane.

Synchronous readback can stall the driver. These runs are untimed diagnostics;
do not include the capture in benchmark intervals or reuse its FPS as evidence.
At 2976 × 1672 the raw plane is 4,975,872 texels / 19,903,488 bytes. The bounded
utility limit is 16,777,216 texels, sufficient for this run. Keep captures ignored.

## Utility API and evidence interpretation

Construct a `Contract` from root's verified pins, exact stage/function marker,
native dimensions, actual global arm, matched camera/scene receipt and complete
other-control receipt excluding only the authorized global enable change.
`Draw` carries the actual source/program association, transformed hashes,
pipeline generation/frame/draw ordinal, linked values and settled hook facts.
These supplied facts must be established by root's actual hook/receipts; record
constructors do not certify a caller's assertions.

Call `inspect(contract, draw, texture, fullDepth, restoration, readbackReturned)`
after restoration. Alternatively, `rawCapture(path, contract, draw, texture,
fullDepth, restoration, readbackReturned)` combines guards, summary and raw write
in a Gson-serializable `Capture` record. Save contract/draw/texture/states plus
returned `Summary` in the caller's JSON. `writeRaw` writes an exact new f32le file with length/hash/
format metadata and refuses overwrite. Save that metadata with the JSON, then
replay summaries from those original bytes. `Summary` reports all texels,
geometry (`depth < 1`), exact clear (`depth == 1`), bounds, row/column occupancy,
and inside/outside counts. It never estimates coverage from viewport or a few
points. For .75 the nominal native rectangle is 2232 × 1254; any populated pixel
outside it is retained as an adverse observation, including boundary pixels.
Do not add an edge tolerance simply to pass; inspect the source's jitter and
actual boundary data if a contradiction appears.

After both arms individually pass provenance/layout/restoration, call
`compare(offContract, offRawDepth, onContract, onRawDepth)`. It scans both full
planes against the candidate footprint. Geometry must exist outside that region
in the matched scale-1 control and the candidate must still contain geometry.
Only then can clear candidate exterior support
`OBSERVED_MATCHED_SCENE_RESTRICTED_DEPTH_FOOTPRINT`. If the control exterior was
already sky/holes, result is inconclusive; clear pixels alone are not raster
work evidence. This is scene-defined depth footprint evidence, not the precise
geometry draw count, fragment invocation count, shading workload, whole-pack
dynamic correctness, motion quality, total-frame gain or original-native parity.
OFF scale 1 uses fixed TAAU and is not the original-native performance denominator.
